stories.title: Pakistan Army Successfully Conducts Test Launch of Fatah-3 Supersonic Cruise Missile
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Army successfully launched the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile on November 18, 2026, marking a significant advancement in the nation's defence capabilities. The military’s media wing, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), announced the event from Rawalpindi, highlighting that the new weapon system features advanced navigation and propulsion systems. It is designed to engage long-range targets with high precision, lethality, and supersonic speed.

According to the ISPR, the missile will greatly improve the strike reach and operational flexibility of the Pakistan Army’s Rocket Force Command, thereby reinforcing the country's conventional deterrence and overall defence posture. High-ranking military officials, including the Commander Army Rocket Force Command, alongside various armed forces officers, scientists, and engineers, were present to witness the successful test launch.

National leaders offered widespread praise for the achievement. President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, and other services chiefs commended the successful test. They expressed appreciation for the hard work and dedication demonstrated by all the engineers, scientists, and personnel involved in reaching this milestone for Pakistan's defence sector.

This test follows a series of recent military developments in Pakistan, including the October tests of the Fatah-2 hypersonic ballistic missile and an extended version of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile, as well as the November flight test of the indigenously developed Fa'az air-to-air missile. These ongoing advancements underscore the country's continuous focus on upgrading its aerospace and military readiness amid regional security dynamics.

stories.title: International Jurists Question Pakistan Judicial Independence After Constitutional Changes
stories.summary:
The International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) released a critical report on Wednesday regarding Pakistan's judiciary. According to the document, recent constitutional and legislative updates have severely weakened judicial independence in the country. ICJ Secretary-General Santiago Canton stated that the measures have placed the highest courts under executive control, leaving victims of human rights violations without effective legal remedies and removing accountability from the government.

The analysis reviews the high courts, the Supreme Court, and the newly established Federal Constitutional Court under international law standards. The findings arrive one year after the passage of the 27th Amendment in November 2025 and two years following the 26th Amendment in October 2024. These laws altered Supreme Court suo motu powers, capped the chief justice's tenure at three years, granted the prime minister appointment authority, created the Federal Constitutional Court, shifted the military command chain, and provided government officials with immunities.

The ICJ asserts that these cumulative changes violate international obligations such as Article 14 of the ICCPR and the UN Basic Principles on the Independence of the Judiciary. While the ICJ acknowledges that Pakistan's judiciary previously required reform due to opaque appointments and judicial overreach, Canton noted that the government exploited public frustration to establish full control. The organisation recommends revising or repealing the provisions within the 26th and 27th amendments that conflict with international standards.

This institutional shift matters because it eliminates the judiciary's ability to act as an effective check on executive power. Without independent oversight, citizens lack recourse for human rights abuses, undermining democratic governance and the rule of law in Pakistan.

stories.title: Islamabad High Court Orders Medical Care and Cleanliness for Bushra Bibi
stories.summary:
The Islamabad High Court directed prison authorities on Wednesday to provide jailed former first lady Bushra Bibi with comprehensive medical facilities, including specialist treatment if needed, and to guarantee proper hygiene in her cell. A division bench comprising Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif issued the order during a hearing regarding appeals filed by Bushra and her husband, former prime minister Imran Khan, against their convictions in the £190 million case. Imran Khan, 73, has been incarcerated since August 2023 following multiple convictions that he and his political party maintain are politically motivated, stemming from legal proceedings that began after his ouster via a no-confidence vote in April 2022.

During the proceedings, Advocate Latif Khosa presented a fresh health application concerning Bushra Bibi's eyesight, warning that her condition could severely deteriorate. Khosa also claimed that seven small snakes had been discovered in her prison cell, which were allegedly killed by a jail official named Sabtain before the area was cemented, while further alleging severe uncleanliness in the facility. In response, Chief Justice Dogar stated that medical care would be provided under existing jail rules and instructed legal counsel to proceed with arguments on the main appeals.

Subsequently, Barrister Salman Safdar began arguments on behalf of Imran Khan, who received a 14-year prison sentence and a Rs1 million fine from an accountability court, while Bushra Bibi was handed a seven-year sentence and a Rs500,000 fine for abetment. Safdar requested that the appeal proceedings be live-streamed, pointing to prior legal precedents, and asked for two weeks to thoroughly review the case records. The court ultimately granted a seven-day preparation period and scheduled the appeals for a hearing after a week.

The underlying Al-Qadir Trust case centers around allegations that Imran Khan and other associates in 2019 adjusted Rs50 billion, equivalent to £190 million at the time, which was sent by Britain's National Crime Agency to the Pakistani government during his premiership. The funds related to a property tycoon's assets seized by the NCA, which maintained the matter was civil and did not indicate guilt. However, the National Accountability Bureau filed a reference in December 2023, leading to charges on February 27, 2024, for approving a confidential agreement without disclosing its details.

stories.title: Pakistan Successfully Test-Fires Fatah-3 Supersonic Cruise Missile
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Army successfully carried out the launch of the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile on November 18, 2026, according to an official statement by the military's media wing, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR). This test represents a major milestone in strengthening Pakistan's national defence sector, utilizing a weapon system built with advanced navigation and propulsion technology capable of striking distant targets with high lethality and precision at supersonic speeds.

ISPR noted that the new missile will bolster the operational flexibility and strike range of the Pakistan Army’s Rocket Force Command, reinforcing the nation's conventional deterrence capabilities. The test was observed by the commander of the Army Rocket Force Command, various senior military officers, engineers, and scientists. Top civilian and military leadership, including President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, and Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, along with other services chiefs, congratulated the development team for their commitment.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also congratulated the nation, describing the test as a major advancement in the country's defence capabilities. This event follows several other recent missile tests by Pakistan's armed forces, such as the Fatah-2 hypersonic ballistic missile and the extended-range Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile tested in October, alongside the flight test of the country's first indigenously developed air-to-air missile, Fa’az, earlier in November.

The successful test comes amid various domestic news topics in Pakistan, including judicial pleas concerning former Prime Minister Imran Khan's medical treatment at Adiala jail, political commentary from figures like Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, and broader international and regional discussions involving military leadership and foreign counterparts.

stories.title: Trump's Board of Peace Criticizes Israel and Hamas Over Gaza Conflict
stories.summary:
The body overseeing US President Donald Trump’s plan to end the war in Gaza has released a 12-page report accusing both Israel and Hamas of failing to fulfill their commitments to halt hostilities. Published ahead of a scheduled United Nations Security Council meeting in New York at the end of November, the report warns that the fragile ceasefire, which has been in place for 13 months, is in danger of collapsing and leaving the local population in severe conditions.

While the ceasefire successfully halted major fighting, the broader peace plan—which entails Hamas disarming, Israeli forces withdrawing, and reconstruction beginning—has remained largely stalled. Although Hamas agreed in July to a roadmap to surrender weapons and transfer governance to a civilian transitional authority, Israel rejected the plan, stating it will not withdraw until Hamas is completely dismantled. The report criticizes Israel for continuing near-daily strikes and displaying an "absence of decisions" regarding a civilian Palestinian police force, while also noting that Hamas fighters have continued attacks and collected taxes that restrict basic commodities.

Gaza's population of more than two million Palestinians remains confined to about a third of the territory, largely living in makeshift tents and damaged infrastructure. The report highlights that Israeli restrictions on supplies and equipment, combined with funding shortfalls, have severely hindered preparation and response capabilities for seasonal flooding, which recently inundated displacement camps. Meanwhile, senior Hamas official Basem Naim dismissed the report as disinformation, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office did not immediately respond.

The Gaza conflict began after Hamas-led attacks from Gaza in October 2023 killed around 1,200 people in Israel. Subsequent Israeli military operations have killed 74,000 Palestinians. Since the US-mediated ceasefire was implemented in October 2025, more than 1,600 Palestinians and five Israeli soldiers have been killed in Gaza, underscoring the ongoing volatility of the region.

stories.title: Pakistan Army Test-Fires Fatah-3 Supersonic Cruise Missile in New Defense Milestone
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Army has successfully conducted a test launch of the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile, marking a notable advancement in the nation's military capabilities, according to an announcement by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR). Equipped with sophisticated propulsion and navigation systems, the weapon is designed to strike distant targets with high lethality, precision, and supersonic speed.

Military officials report that the introduction of the Fatah-3 will significantly expand the operational flexibility and strike reach of the Pakistan Army’s Rocket Force Command. This development is expected to further strengthen the country's overall conventional deterrence and national defense posture moving forward.

The test launch was attended by senior officers of the Pakistan Armed Forces, the Commander of the Army Rocket Force Command, and various project engineers and scientists who contributed to the system's development.

Following the test, top national leaders including the President, Prime Minister, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, and other services chiefs offered their commendations. They praised the dedication and commitment of all personnel involved in achieving this latest milestone in Pakistan's defense sector.

stories.title: Pakistan Considers 14-Province Administrative Reform Proposal
stories.summary:
Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal stated that a proposal regarding the creation of 14 provinces in Pakistan is under discussion. According to the plan, Punjab would have four provinces, Sindh four, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa three, and Balochistan three. Furthermore, discussions have taken place regarding granting Islamabad separate provincial status. Iqbal revealed that he wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in September, suggesting the creation of a committee to review the debate surrounding new provinces, though no progress has been made yet.

Regarding the administration of the capital, Iqbal noted that the prime minister tasked him with formulating an alternative model. After reviewing global capitals, officials proposed a hybrid system combining local government and a provincial assembly. This model envisions a legislative forum for Islamabad consisting of roughly 25 members, including 21 general seats, three reserved for women, and one for minorities. Additionally, union councils could be established as an elected third tier later on, and boundaries might expand to include parts of Rawalpindi division.

Iqbal emphasized that the issue of forming additional provinces must be addressed prior to the Senate elections scheduled for March 2027. He warned that establishing new provinces afterward could lead to disputes regarding proportionate representation in the 96-member upper house for a period of six years. He also dismissed rumors concerning the introduction of a presidential system, noting no serious proposals exist.

Urging politicians to take charge of the debate instead of remaining evasive, Iqbal pointed out the necessity of administrative reforms. He noted that following the eighteenth amendment, provinces failed to devolve functions, resulting in top-heavy provincial structures. The discussion aims to address these structural issues within the country's governance framework.

stories.title: Pakistan commands 227-run lead against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi Test
stories.summary:
Pakistan seized firm control of the second Test against Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Wednesday. At stumps on day two, Sri Lanka stumbled to 74-3 in their second innings, still trailing by 153 runs with only seven wickets remaining. Earlier, Pakistan were bowled out for 325 in 87.5 overs, establishing a commanding 227-run first-innings lead following Sri Lanka's low score of 98.

Pakistan's lower order rescued the innings after Lahiru Kumara wreaked havoc with a five-wicket haul, finishing with 5-95. Wicket-keeper-batter Ghazi Ghori scored 54 off 90 deliveries before falling to Milan Rathnayaka, while Razaullah contributed a brisk 42 off 32 balls with four fours and three sixes. Overnight batter Azan Awais failed to add to his 47, and Saqib Khan added 37. Asitha Fernando claimed three wickets for the visitors.

Sri Lanka's second innings got off to a disastrous start. Saqib removed Lahiru Udara for seven, and Razaullah trapped Dinesh Chandimal leg-before for a duck to leave the visitors at 10-2. Aamer Jamal then dismissed Kamindu Mendis for 16, reducing Sri Lanka to 39-3. Dhananjaya de Silva, unbeaten on 24, and Pasindu Sooriyabandara, on 18, managed to survive until the close of play.

Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson described his team's batting effort as scrappy but praised the lower-order contributions that built the large lead. Kumara acknowledged that Sri Lanka conceded too many runs in the final session but expressed confidence in his side's batting lineup ahead of day three. Hesson also noted the importance of developing players in various conditions, pointing out that six Pakistan players were currently playing their first or second Test.

stories.title: Xi, Trump, Putin Exchange Greetings in Shenzhen Ahead of Trilateral Summit
stories.summary:
United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin exchanged initial greetings in Shenzhen on Wednesday. The leaders crossed paths ahead of a formal trilateral meeting scheduled for Thursday, with footage showing Putin shaking hands with Trump and both men exchanging pleasantries with Xi before posing for a group photo at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

Xi personally welcomed Trump upon his arrival at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport on Wednesday, with the two leaders sharing a brief hug. Xi told Trump he looked forward to an in-depth exchange on major issues concerning bilateral relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape. Thursday's trilateral meeting has raised international concerns that the three leaders might make decisions regarding Ukraine without Kyiv and European nations, or attempt to establish 21st-century spheres of influence. Although Washington initially indicated Ukraine would not be addressed, Trump later stated that it would be discussed.

Security remains high for the Apec gathering in China's southern Guangdong province, where discussions are also expected to cover the Iran war and nuclear disarmament. Earlier on Wednesday, Xi met with Putin for their fifth meeting of the year, emphasizing closer ties across government, legislative, and military bodies. Russian officials stated that Putin and Xi would discuss energy, finance, and foreign policy matters including Ukraine and North Korea.

Putin struck a defiant tone regarding Western sanctions following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, stating they had failed and calling for unity and dialogue. Meanwhile, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney warned that sanctions would continue as long as the war persists. Trump's visit to China follows a stop in the Philippines, where he met with Quad leaders and attended an ASEAN summit.

stories.title: راولپنڈی ٹیسٹ: پاکستان کو سری لنکا کے خلاف 153 رنز کی برتری حاصل
stories.summary:
راولپنڈی میں کھیلے جانے والے دوسرے ٹیسٹ میچ کے دوسرے روز کا کھیل ختم ہونے پر پاکستان نے سری لنکا کے خلاف 153 رنز کی برتری حاصل کر لی ہے۔ دوسرے دن کے اختتام تک سری لنکا نے اپنی دوسری اننگز میں تین وکٹوں کے نقصان پر 74 رنز بنائے تھے۔ اس وقت کریز پر پسندو سوریا بندارا اور دھننجایا ڈی سلوا موجود ہیں اور دونوں کے درمیان 35 رنز کی شراکت قائم ہے۔ پاکستان کی جانب سے دوسری اننگز میں ثاقب خان، رضا اللہ اور عامر جمال نے ایک ایک کھلاڑی کو آؤٹ کیا۔

دوسرے روز کے آغاز پر پاکستان نے پہلی اننگز میں 325 رنز بنا کر 227 رنز کی برتری حاصل کی تھی۔ پاکستان کی پہلی اننگز میں وکٹ کیپر غازی غوری نے ٹیسٹ کرکٹ میں اپنی پہلی نصف سنچری اسکور کی جبکہ رضا اللہ نے چار چوکوں اور تین چھکوں کی مدد سے 42 رنز بنائے۔ اس کے علاوہ اوپنر آذان اویس نے 47، سعود شکیل نے 24، نائٹ واچ مین ثاقب خان نے 37 اور سلمان آغا نے 21 رنز اسکور کیے۔ سری لنکا کی پہلی اننگز محض 98 رنز پر ڈھیر ہو گئی تھی جس میں محمد عباس، رضا اللہ اور عامر جمال نے تین تین جبکہ ثاقب خان نے ایک وکٹ حاصل کی تھی۔

راولپنڈی کے اس گراؤنڈ میں سری لنکا کا یہ پہلی اننگز کا سکور پاکستان کے خلاف کسی بھی اننگز میں چوتھا سب سے کم سکور ہے۔ میچ کے دوران پاکستانی فاسٹ بولرز کی کارکردگی کو سوشل میڈیا پر شائقین اور کرکٹ تجزیہ کاروں کی جانب سے بھرپور سراہا گیا ہے۔ تجزیہ کاروں نے پچ کی مشکل صورتحال میں بیٹرز کو ذمہ داری سے کھیلنے کا مشورہ دیا ہے جبکہ بابر اعظم کی کپتانی اور فیصلہ سازی کی بھی تعریف کی گئی ہے۔

واضح رہے کہ دونوں ٹیموں کے درمیان راولپنڈی میں کھیلا جانے والا پہلا ٹیسٹ میچ بے نتیجہ ختم ہو چکا ہے، اس لیے یہ دوسرا ٹیسٹ میچ جیتنے والی ٹیم سیریز اپنے نام کرنے میں کامیاب ہو جائے گی۔ میچ کے دوران پاکستان کے بولرز نے ایک بار پھر اپنی سیم اور باؤنس کے ذریعے مخالف بلے بازوں کو شدید مشکلات میں مبتلا رکھا۔

stories.title: تھیٹر پروڈیوسرز خواتین آرٹسٹوں کو نازیبا لباس پر مجبور کرتے ہیں: عظمیٰ بخاری
stories.summary:
صوبائی وزیر اطلاعات پنجاب عظمیٰ بخاری نے پنجاب اسمبلی میں اظہار خیال کرتے ہوئے انکشاف کیا ہے کہ اسٹیج آرٹسٹ خواتین کا کہنا ہے کہ پروڈیوسرز انھیں نازیبا لباس پہننے پر مجبور کرتے ہیں۔ انھوں نے کہا کہ انھوں نے ایسے ایسے واقعات سنے ہیں جنہیں بیان نہیں کیا جا سکتا اور نہ ہی کوئی انھیں سن سکتا ہے۔ ان کا کہنا تھا کہ آج تک ہمارے ہاں کسی بھی آرٹسٹ کو اس کی محنت کا پورا معاوضہ نہیں ملتا۔

عظمیٰ بخاری نے مزید کہا کہ حکومت نے تھیٹر کے معیار کو بہتر بنانے کے لیے جو بل پیش کیا تھا اسے سب کے ساتھ شیئر کیا جا چکا ہے۔ ان کا کہنا تھا کہ ماضی میں جہیز کی لعنت اور منشیات کے خلاف ڈرامے بنتے تھے جنہیں لوگ شوق سے دیکھتے تھے۔ صوبائی وزیر نے سوال اٹھایا کہ سہیل احمد، خالد عباس ڈار اور وسیم عباس جیسے نامور فنکاروں نے تھیٹر کیوں چھوڑا، اور اس معاملے پر اب بحث ہو چکی ہے لہذا بل کی منظوری وقت کی اہم ضرورت ہے۔

ان کا یہ بھی کہنا تھا کہ یہ تاثر غلط تھا کہ ڈراما ناچ گانے کے بغیر نہیں چل سکتا، کیونکہ الحمرا میں بغیر ناچ گانے کے اسٹیج ڈراما مسلسل تین دن کامیاب رہا۔ عظمیٰ بخاری نے واضح کیا کہ جو لوگ تھیٹر میں فحاشی پھیلا رہے ہیں وہ دراصل گھس بیٹھیے ہیں اور اصل آرٹسٹ نہیں ہیں۔

حکومت کے مؤقف کی وضاحت کرتے ہوئے صوبائی وزیر نے کہا کہ حکومت تھیٹر پر کسی قسم کی پابندی عائد کرنے کا ارادہ نہیں رکھتی بلکہ اسے ایک منظم طریقے سے مانیٹر کرنا چاہتی ہے۔ اسمبلی میں اس بحث کے دوران اپوزیشن کے اعتراضات پر بھی بات کی گئی جبکہ اجلاس میں دیگر سیاسی و سماجی امور پر بھی مختلف رہنماؤں نے اپنے خیالات کا اظہار کیا۔

stories.title: الیکشن کمیشن ذرائع کا بلاول بھٹو کے پریس کانفرنس کے بیان پر ردعمل
stories.summary:
ذرائع الیکشن کمیشن نے پاکستان پیپلز پارٹی کے چیئرمین بلاول بھٹو زرداری کی میٹ دی پریس کے دوران دیے گئے بیان پر اپنا ردعمل ظاہر کیا ہے۔ ذرائع کا کہنا ہے کہ بلاول بھٹو کے بیان میں انتخابی معاملات سے متعلق بنیادی حقائق کو یکسر نظرانداز کیا گیا ہے۔ الیکشن کمیشن کے مطابق مخصوص نشستیں صرف انہی سیاسی جماعتوں کا حق بنتی ہیں جو باقاعدہ طور پر بطور جماعت انتخابات میں حصہ لیتی ہیں اور ان پر لازم ہوتا ہے کہ وہ الیکشن سے پہلے مقررہ مدت کے اندر امیدواروں کی ترجیحی فہرست جمع کروائیں۔

ذرائع کے مطابق پاکستان تحریک انصاف کی جانب سے ایسی کوئی بھی ترجیحی فہرست الیکشن کمیشن میں جمع نہیں کروائی گئی تھی۔ اس کے علاوہ، بلاول بھٹو کی جانب سے تحریک انصاف سے انتخابی نشان واپس لینے کے حکم کو غیر قانونی قرار دینے کے معاملے پر بھی ذرائع نے وضاحت کی ہے۔ ان کا کہنا ہے کہ الیکشنز ایکٹ 2017ء کے سیکشن 208 اور 209 کے تحت ہر سیاسی جماعت کے لیے شفاف انداز میں انٹرا پارٹی انتخابات کرانا لازمی قانونی تقاضا ہے۔

الیکشن کمیشن کے ذرائع کا مزید کہنا ہے کہ تحریک انصاف مقررہ قانونی معیار اور اپنے ہی منظور شدہ پارٹی آئین کے مطابق انٹرا پارٹی انتخابات کرانے میں ناکام رہی ہے۔ اسی پس منظر میں پی ٹی آئی کو انتخابی نشان سے متعلق فیصلے کا سامنا کرنا پڑا۔

یاد رہے کہ سیاسی رہنماؤں کی جانب سے الیکشن کمیشن کے فیصلوں اور انتخابی عمل پر وقتاً فوقتاً تبصرے کیے جاتے رہے ہیں، جن پر متعلقہ اداروں کی طرف سے آئینی اور قانونی حقائق کی روشنی میں ردعمل سامنے آتا ہے۔

stories.title: پاکستان کا فتح-3 سپرسونک کروز میزائل کا کامیاب تجربہ، آئی ایس پی آر
stories.summary:
پاک فوج کے شعبہ تعلقات عامہ (آئی ایس پی آر) کے مطابق پاکستان نے فتح 3 سپر سونک کروز میزائل کا کامیاب تجربہ کر لیا ہے۔ یہ میزائل جدید ترین نیویگیشن اور پروپلشن سسٹمز سے مکمل طور پر لیس ہے۔ اس میزائل کی خاص بات یہ ہے کہ یہ سپرسونک رفتار کے ساتھ طویل فاصلے تک موجود اہداف کو انتہائی درستی اور مہارت کے ساتھ نشانہ بنانے کی مکمل صلاحیت رکھتا ہے۔

آئی ایس پی آر نے بتایا ہے کہ فتح-3 کی شمولیت سے پاکستان آرمی کی راکٹ فورس کمانڈ کی آپریشنل لچک اور اسٹرائیک رینج میں نمایاں اضافہ ہوگا۔ اس اہم تجربے سے ملک کی مجموعی روایتی دفاعی صلاحیتیں اور دفاعی پوزیشن مزید زیادہ مستحکم اور مضبوط ہو جائیں گی۔ اس لانچنگ کے موقع پر کمانڈر آرمی راکٹ فورس کمانڈ، مسلح افواج کے سینئر افسران کے ساتھ ساتھ میزائل تیار کرنے والے سائنسدانوں اور انجینئرز نے بھی خصوصی طور پر شرکت کی۔

فتح-3 کے کامیاب تجربے پر ملک کی اعلیٰ ترین قیادت نے مسرت کا اظہار کیا ہے۔ صدر آصف زرداری، وزیراعظم شہباز شریف، چیف آف ڈیفنس فورسز اور تمام سروسز چیفس نے اس شاندار کامیابی پر مبارکباد پیش کی ہے۔

سیاسی و عسکری قیادت نے قومی دفاعی صلاحیتوں کو مزید ترقی دینے کے اس سنگ میل کو حاصل کرنے میں دن رات کام کرنے والے تمام افراد کی انتھک لگن، محنت اور عزم کو بھرپور انداز میں سراہا ہے۔

stories.title: Israel's Parliament Elects New Speaker to Undo Netanyahu Legislative Legacy
stories.summary:
Israel’s parliament convened on Wednesday under a newly elected speaker belonging to the anti-Benjamin Netanyahu bloc, initiating a legislative offensive to roll back the caretaker prime minister's policies. Matan Kahana, an ally of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, secured the position late Tuesday with 66 votes out of 120, backed by Arab-majority lists that gained significant seats in the October 27 election.

The speaker position controls the parliamentary timetable, enabling Eisenkot's camp to accelerate or delay debates and target Netanyahu’s legislative agenda before a new government is formed. High on the agenda is repealing reforms that reduced judicial independence, which Netanyahu advanced amid ongoing corruption charges that could lead to prison time if he loses power. A provisional committee began examining fast-track bills on Wednesday to reverse legislation that increased political influence over the judiciary and media.

Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu secured a clear majority in the October election. Netanyahu acknowledged the outcome on Tuesday, stating it reflects the will of the people and calling for unity. Netanyahu has reportedly urged US President Donald Trump to resume war on Iran while emphasizing the necessity of a unity government. Aside from reversing judicial reforms, Eisenkot has vowed to swiftly establish a state commission of inquiry into security failures surrounding the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack.

stories.title: PTI's Political Position is Finally Being Recognized, Says Barrister Gohar
stories.summary:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar stated on Wednesday that he was pleased the party's political position is finally being recognized, though he was unsure of the motives behind recent statements by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari. Speaking to the media, Gohar emphasized that PTI does not believe in power-sharing and asserted that all party decisions are made under the guidance and consultation of the PTI founder.

Gohar cautioned against issuing irresponsible statements regarding the formation of new provinces and the distribution of resources. He added that PTI has kept its political strategy concealed and does not wish to be a beneficiary of the current system. His remarks follow an address by Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari at the Karachi Press Club's Meet the Press programme.

During his address in Karachi, Bilawal urged the government to revive dialogue with opposition parties, including the PTI, and to put an end to political victimization. The PPP leader emphasized the importance of acknowledging political realities and formally recognized the political stake held by the PTI.

stories.title: Iran Fires at Kuwait and Bahrain Amid Broadening Regional Hostilities
stories.summary:
Iran targeted US drone and missile sites in Kuwait overnight following a United States strike on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The military action marked Tehran's first attack on the US-allied Gulf state since September. Concurrently, Bahrain announced it intercepted Iranian aerial attacks for the third time in a week, condemning what it termed a systematic hostile approach toward the kingdom, which hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet.

The exchange follows US airstrikes on Tuesday evening, when American fighter aircraft hit a missile launch site on Qeshm Island in retaliation for previous Iranian attacks on US personnel and assets. An Iranian official stated the US strike caused no infrastructure damage. Meanwhile, Kuwait asserted its right to protect its sovereignty and vital facilities. In state media videos, Iranian Army Commander-in-Chief Amir Hatami warned the United States against further escalation, threatening a stronger response without geographic limitations.

This ongoing conflict, which began on February 28 when the US and Israel attacked Iran, has severely disrupted global shipping, increased energy prices, and expanded across the Middle East. Fighting has drawn in Lebanon through Hezbollah, Yemen through Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities, and Jordan where US forces were targeted. Additionally, an LNG tanker off Oman was abandoned, and a UAE vessel was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, leaving one crew member missing and eleven injured. Diplomatic efforts continue, with Qatari and Iranian officials meeting recently to bridge gaps, while Saudi Arabia urged a return to negotiations and international law.

Tensions also touched Washington on Tuesday when President Trump noted the US was taking seriously intelligence regarding a potential Iranian plot involving a dirty bomb. However, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated on Wednesday that he did not view the threat to the capital as imminent. Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly denied these allegations, dismissing them as baseless.

stories.title: Woman Killed and Two Injured by Fallen High-Voltage Power Line in Turbat
stories.summary:
A woman died and her husband and son sustained critical burn injuries when an 11,000-volt power line snapped and fell on their home in the Wasto Bazaar area of Turbat during the early hours of Wednesday. The high-tension wire electrocuted the family members, who were subsequently transported to the Teaching Hospital Turbat. Hospital staff and attendants reported that the injured faced severe difficulties receiving proper care because the facility's burns unit was non-functional. The deceased was identified as Mah Bibi, wife of Muhammad Ismail.

Snapped overhead power cables have become a recurring hazard in Turbat and surrounding locations. Local residents noted that similar accidents involving live wires during operational hours have previously occurred in Wasto Bazaar, Malikabad, Shahi Tump, and regions under the Mirani Dam feeder. Expressing deep concern over the performance of the Quetta Electric Supply Company (Qesco), citizens have demanded immediate repairs and safe installations for power lines crossing residential areas to prevent additional fatalities.

This incident follows several similar electrocution tragedies across Pakistan in recent months. Earlier in November, three members of a single family died in Bahawalnagar when a transmission line fell on their home. In June, eight participants of a mourning procession were killed in Shikarpur district after a religious flag contacted a high-tension wire, and two people died from fallen 11kV cables in Larkana in May.

This recurring issue highlights critical infrastructure and safety failures in power distribution networks across Pakistan. The lack of prompt maintenance and non-functional medical infrastructure, such as the burns unit in Turbat, severely exacerbates the danger and impact of these infrastructure accidents on local communities.

stories.title: Pakistan Begins Thar Coal Mining Electrification Project to Cut Costs
stories.summary:
The Pakistani government has formally commenced work on transitioning Thar coal mining operations from diesel generators to the national grid. Announced during a review meeting chaired by Federal Minister for Power Sardar Awais Ahmad Khan Leghari, the project's completion target has been advanced by eight to nine months to the first quarter of 2028, specifically by April 2028. Representatives from the Thar Coal and Energy Board (TCEB), Sindh Engro Coal Mining Company (SECMC), Sino Sindh Resources Limited (SSRL), the Power Division, and Hyderabad Electric Supply Company (HESCO) attended the session.

The initiative connects mining operations in Thar Block I and Block II to the grid via 132kV transmission infrastructure from the Islamkot Grid Station, supplying approximately 60 megawatts of electricity. Currently, mining operations consume between 200,000 and 250,000 litres of diesel daily, including about 35,000 litres used solely for dewatering. Diesel-based power generation costs around 33 cents per kilowatt-hour, whereas grid electricity will reduce this expense to 13 cents, marking a reduction of over 60 percent.

The transition is projected to save Pakistan between $25 million and $30 million annually in foreign exchange, with daily diesel savings estimated at roughly Rs25 million. Furthermore, coal production costs and the resulting coal tariff are expected to drop by about $0.70 per tonne, lowering the overall power basket cost. In addition to financial benefits, carbon emissions will decline by approximately 80,000 tonnes per year. Diesel-powered mining vehicles are also being progressively converted to electric systems, with Block I planning to introduce about 40 electric trucks by the end of the year and Block II aiming for EV deployment in 2028.

This infrastructure upgrade is significant because Thar coal serves as a cornerstone of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor and plays a vital role in national energy security. By reducing reliance on expensive imported diesel, the project aims to stabilize energy tariffs and support long-term decarbonization goals.

stories.title: Copper Prices Plunge to Seven-Month Low Amid Inflation Fears and Selloff
stories.summary:
Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange experienced a sharp decline on Wednesday, falling 3.5% to reach $12,770 a metric ton by 1100 GMT. Earlier in the session, the metal hit its lowest value since April 13 at $12,700, marking its fifth consecutive session of losses. This steep drop was driven by speculative selling, inflation worries, and a strong dollar, which breached key technical support levels and prompted automated computer-driven funds to unload holdings. In the United States, Comex copper futures similarly decreased by 3.8% to hit a seven-month low of $5.76 per pound.

The broader market downturn also affected other industrial metals. Aluminium on the London Metal Exchange dropped 2.2% to $2,869 a ton, touching nearly a one-year low, while zinc fell 1.4% to $3,623 a ton. Lead lost 0.4% to finish at $1,864, nickel decreased by 2.5% to $16,055, and tin suffered a severe 7.1% plunge to $41,840, marking an eight-month low. These declines occurred alongside a steady US dollar, supported by positive economic data and Federal Reserve commentary that fueled expectations of potential interest rate hikes.

The widespread selloff occurred despite strong localized demand in top consumer China, where import premiums surged to a record high of $360 a ton. Market analysts noted that macroeconomic pressures, including concerns over higher funding costs and previous technology and artificial intelligence sector pullbacks impacting data center projects, weighed heavily on overall investor sentiment and overshadowed regional supply shortages.

stories.title: Bangladesh Wicketkeeper Litton Das Sets New Test Record Against South Africa
stories.summary:
Bangladesh wicketkeeper Litton Das established a new world Test record for the most dismissals in a single innings during the fourth day of the first Test in South Africa on Wednesday. Das secured a total of eight dismissals by adding two stumpings to his six catches earlier in the match. His record-breaking performance included removing South African batsman Ryan Rickelton for 102 and Kagiso Rabada for a career-best 72 off the bowling of off-spinner Mehidy Hasan. By achieving eight dismissals, Das surpassed the previous record of seven, which was jointly held by Pakistan's Wasim Bari, England's Bob Taylor, New Zealand's Ian Smith, and West Indians Ridley Jacobs and Joshua Da Silva.

Despite Das's historic effort, South Africa managed to build a commanding 157-run first innings lead by posting a total of 557 in response to Bangladesh's initial 400 runs. The home side capitalized on a prolific 117-run eighth-wicket partnership between Rickelton and Rabada during an extended morning session that yielded 171 runs for the final three wickets. Das also had a missed opportunity earlier in the contest, having dropped Rickelton when he was on nought on Monday.

The South African lower order continued to punish the visiting bowling attack as the innings concluded. Captain Temba Bavuma returned to the crease after retiring hurt with a calf injury on Tuesday to finish unbeaten on 68. He was joined by last man Dane Paterson, who contributed a quick 29 runs to a final-wicket partnership of 45 runs before South Africa's innings finally came to a close.

stories.title: India States Air India Flight Crash Investigation Nears Final Stages
stories.summary:
The Indian government announced on Wednesday that the official investigation into the Air India plane crash that claimed 260 lives last year is currently in its final stage. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta informed the Supreme Court of the progress during a hearing concerning a petition filed by Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, the father of the flight's captain, Sumeet Sabharwal. The petitioner has been seeking a separate, independent inquiry into the disaster. Mehta requested a two-to-three-week adjournment from the court, emphasizing that authorities are adhering to global protocols without intentional delays.

The tragic accident occurred on June 12, 2025, when an Air India Boeing 787 Dreamliner crashed into a residential neighborhood near the airport shortly after takeoff from Ahmedabad bound for London. The disaster resulted in the deaths of 241 out of the 242 individuals on board, alongside 19 people on the ground. A preliminary report released in July 2025 indicated that the aircraft's engine fuel-control switches had shifted from the 'run' to the 'cutoff' position seconds after departure, starving both engines of fuel, though the report could not determine why the switches moved.

The investigation has faced scrutiny and criticism from the captain's father, who alleged that officials from the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau implied during a home visit that his son deliberately cut the fuel supply. Previously, the AAIB informed the court that it had completed a cockpit voice recorder transcript and a psychological autopsy. Authorities anticipated distributing a draft final report around October to participating countries for feedback prior to its formal finalization and publication.

stories.title: US Government Faces Tech Outages as Trump Administration Dismisses Concerns
stories.summary:
A series of technology disruptions that recently grounded thousands of flights and disabled corporate email systems expanded to the US National Security Agency on Tuesday. The NSA reported that its network encountered a temporary degradation during routine maintenance activities, though mission-critical capabilities continued to function normally. These persistent technical failures, which also impacted the banking sector earlier in the week, have sparked demands for transparency from lawmakers, including Republican Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri, who questioned whether the sequence of events was merely coincidental.

President Donald Trump downplayed the significance of the incidents while attending Association of Southeast Asian Nations meetings in Manila, attributing the disruptions to the natural complexities of large and powerful organizations with substantial financial resources. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who also serves as the national security adviser, described the outages as unsettling but asserted that the occurrences were completely independent of one another. Rubio emphasized to reporters that there is zero evidence pointing to malicious actors and confirmed that the nation is not facing a systemic attack.

stories.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Begins Global Rollout After 13-Year Wait
stories.summary:
The highly anticipated video game Grand Theft Auto VI is officially launching globally, starting at midnight in individual markets like New Zealand. Developed by Rockstar Games, a subsidiary of Take-Two Interactive, and played on Microsoft's Xbox Series X and S alongside Sony's PlayStation 5, the new installment arrives after 13 years of development and production costs estimated at $1 billion or more.

Set in Vice City, a fictional portrayal of Miami in Leonida, the narrative follows romantic partners and criminals Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval. The game offers activities such as visiting nightclubs, gun stores, zoos, and scuba diving. Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimated early sales of nearly 16 million copies totaling over $1.5 billion ahead of the release. Some fans have taken time off work or planned all-night gaming sessions to dive in immediately.

Tore Olsson, a history professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, noted that the title might be less provocative than previous versions, potentially encouraging ethical play styles. Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North, indicated that indiscriminate carnage would not align with the narrative of a struggling young couple. Completion of the main game is expected to take around 50 hours.

The franchise originated in 1997 with basic graphics and car-stealing missions that drew criticism from politicians and parents while appealing to players. Subsequent iterations, such as 2013's Grand Theft Auto V set in Los Santos, grew significantly more sophisticated and commercially successful. Excitement for the latest release has driven strong pre-launch metrics and widespread fan engagement globally.

stories.title: Ben Duckett Scores Century as England Defeats Australia in ODI
stories.summary:
England secured a 97-run victory over Australia in the third one-day international in Hobart on Wednesday, capturing the series win. After dropping the opening match in Perth, England rebounded strongly in Adelaide and maintained control by scoring 328 runs and bowling out the hosts for 231 in the 46th over. English captain Harry Brook won the toss and elected to bat first.

Ben Duckett anchored the innings with an undefeated performance, hitting a seventh ODI century off 94 balls that included 13 fours and one six. Will Jacks supported with 59 runs, while opener Tom Banton added 44. Australia's run chase faltered early after losing openers Travis Head and captain Mitchell Marsh within the first two overs. Josh Inglis was dismissed shortly after, leaving the team struggling at 34-3.

Matt Renshaw attempted to stabilize the innings with 55 runs before being caught and bowled by spinner Liam Dawson. Alex Carey was run out for 37, and Cameron Green retired hurt after sustaining a blow to the mouth. Renshaw finished with 3-51 and Jack Edwards claimed 4-31 for Australia, but the home side failed to mount a successful challenge against the visitors.

The match took place amidst ongoing scrutiny surrounding historical ball-tampering allegations in Australian cricket. England's aggressive batting and effective bowling performance ensured they clinched the series decisively following their earlier win in Adelaide.

stories.title: NASA Voyager 1 Reaches Historic Milestone of One Light-Day
stories.summary:
NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft has reached a distance of one light-day from Earth, equating to approximately 16 billion miles or 26 billion kilometers, based on advance calculations by the US space agency. Launched in 1977, the robotic probe crossed the threshold on Wednesday at 5:16 a.m. ET. Officials at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California anticipated a delay of about a day to receive confirmation signals and scheduled an event to discuss the achievement.

Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd expressed amazement at the milestone, noting that the spacecraft travels at nearly 38,000 miles per hour. In 2012, Voyager 1 crossed the outer edge of the heliosphere to enter interstellar space, while its twin, Voyager 2, launched also in 1977 and entered interstellar space in 2018. Power-saving measures are projected to maintain communication capabilities for another three to four years.

The mission aims to continue scientific observations through the 50th launch anniversary next year, powered by instruments measuring magnetic fields, cosmic rays, and plasma waves. Data is transmitted to Earth whenever NASA's Deep Space Network points its giant radio antennas toward the spacecraft. Researchers are tracking ongoing phenomena, including the direction of magnetic fields and pressure fronts generated by solar storms.

Earlier in its mission, Voyager 1 flew past Jupiter and Saturn, the solar system's two largest planets. Scientists continue to analyze data to determine the boundaries of the sun's influence and the characteristics of pristine interstellar space.

stories.title: Pakistani Rupee Edges Up Against US Dollar in Inter-Bank Market
stories.summary:
The Pakistani rupee registered a marginal increase against the US dollar during Wednesday's inter-bank trading session. The local currency closed at 276.55, marking a rise of Re0.01 compared to the previous day's close of 276.56 against the greenback.

Internationally, the US dollar remained near a 19-month high supported by recent economic data and Federal Reserve comments indicating potential interest rate hikes. The dollar index rose 0.05% to 103.66, having touched 103.78 overnight, its highest level since April 2, 2025. Conversely, the euro and the British pound experienced slight declines, while the Japanese yen weakened despite strong export figures.

Investors continue anticipating a quarter-point rate hike by the Federal Reserve in December to address inflation, with CME FedWatch tools reflecting these expectations. Focus remains on upcoming US housing starts data and the release of minutes from the central bank's previous meeting.

Oil prices declined on Wednesday following data indicating a rise in US crude and fuel inventories. Brent crude futures fell 0.7% to $92.53 a barrel, and US West Texas Intermediate futures dropped 1.4% to $84.77 a barrel, though ongoing geopolitical tensions and shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz limited further losses.

stories.title: Islamabad High Court Orders Medical Care for Bushra Bibi
stories.summary:
The Islamabad High Court has directed prison authorities to guarantee proper medical attention and clean living conditions for Bushra Bibi in accordance with jail regulations. A division bench, consisting of Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif, issued the directive while granting defense counsel seven days to prepare arguments regarding appeals filed by Bushra Bibi and her husband, PTI founder Imran Khan, against their convictions in the £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case.

During the proceedings, the court addressed a miscellaneous application concerning Bushra Bibi's deteriorating eyesight, her need for surgery, potential post-operative complications, and prison medical facilities. Her lawyer, Sardar Latif Khosa, informed the bench that she requires surgery, faces vision risks, and raised concerns about cell hygiene after reporting that seven small snakes were found in her cell and killed by a prison official. Khosa stressed that infection risks following surgery necessitate strict precautions and special medical access under jail rules.

Chief Justice Dogar acknowledged the health concerns and assured the legal team that the former first lady would receive all permissible facilities and remain in safe hands. The court ordered Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Hayat Malik to ensure the implementation of the directives through relevant prison authorities. Additionally, the defense requested that the appeal proceedings be broadcast live due to significant public interest, noting precedents from other high-profile court cases.

Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi were previously sentenced by an Islamabad accountability court on January 17, 2025, receiving 14-year and seven-year prison terms respectively. Defense lawyers recently submitted affidavits detailing a three-hour meeting with the incarcerated couple at Adiala jail on November 11 following earlier court orders. The hearing for the main appeals was subsequently adjourned for seven days to allow counsel to finalize their arguments.

stories.title: Bangladesh Deploys Paramilitary Troops Amid Unrest Over Hasina's Return
stories.summary:
Bangladesh authorities increased security measures and deployed hundreds of paramilitary troops nationwide following a surge of protests, bomb blasts, and arson attacks. The unrest stems from the planned December return of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who has been living in exile in India since fleeing Dhaka during violent protests in August 2024. The government has thus far rejected her requests for a new passport and identity card.

In response to her planned return, supporters of Hasina's banned Awami League party organized rallies and announced a nationwide lockdown for November 19. Over the preceding ten days, police recorded numerous crude bomb blasts and torched vehicles across at least 28 districts, resulting in multiple injuries among civilians and police personnel. Violence escalated further with the reported killing of a ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party activist near Gopalganj, a crude bomb explosion near a cabinet minister's residence, and various arson attacks targeting properties and local shops.

The unrest also impacted institutions linked to Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, who headed the interim government following Hasina's ouster. At least 37 branches and offices of Grameen Bank faced arson attacks or attempted fires since November 10. Additionally, a bus company helper was burnt to death in Pirojpur after two buses were set on fire, coinciding with the one-year anniversary of a local court sentencing Hasina to death for ordering a crackdown during the 2024 student-led uprising.

In response to the escalating violence, Dhaka Metropolitan Police arrested at least 71 members of banned organizations, including the Awami League, over a 24-hour period. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed accused overseas Awami League leaders of inciting supporters to destabilize the country and destroy property, stating that individuals involved in the violence will be prosecuted.

stories.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping Greets US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen
stories.summary:
Chinese President Xi Jinping personally welcomed US President Donald Trump upon his arrival at Shenzhen Baoan International Airport on Wednesday. Trump descended from Air Force One and saluted alongside Xi on a red carpet lined with attendees waving colorful pom-poms and national flags before the two leaders shared a handshake. The US leader traveled to China's southern Guangdong Province to participate in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit.

The high-level arrival precedes a scheduled trilateral meeting in Shenzhen that will also involve Russian President Vladimir Putin. Ahead of the discussions, Xinhua reported that Xi expressed his desire to foster a constructive and strategically stable relationship with the United States. Xi stated that he anticipated an in-depth exchange of views concerning bilateral ties, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape.

According to the Chinese leader, the envisioned relationship should be anchored on the principles of mutual respect, fairness, and reciprocity. The upcoming trilateral gathering between the leaders of China, the United States, and Russia highlights intense diplomatic engagements focusing on major international and regional issues during the summit.

stories.title: Immigration New Zealand Updates Online Portal with Mandatory Passport Scanning
stories.summary:
Immigration New Zealand has updated its online visa application platform to introduce new features designed to streamline submissions and reduce errors. Starting November 23, 2026, individuals applying for Visitor Visas or Accredited Employer Work Visas through the Immigration Online system will be required to upload a digital passport scan. This requirement aligns the submission process with existing procedures already established for students and Permanent Resident Visa applicants.

As part of the upgrade, the system will automatically import key passport details directly into the application form. Applicants are advised to carefully review these pre-filled data fields and correct any mismatches prior to final submission. The initiative aims to enhance processing efficiency and prevent potential travel complications caused by inconsistent information across official travel documents.

Additionally, the upgraded platform will serve as the preferred method for family members of New Zealand citizens or residents to lodge temporary entry visas. Immigration New Zealand will prioritize applications processed through this new framework. Users with saved drafts in legacy systems can choose to complete them in the older format or restart using the updated platform, while older applications submitted before November 15, 2026, will continue to be processed normally without requiring additional steps.

stories.title: Malaysian Palm Oil Futures Slide More Than One Percent on Weak Demand
stories.summary:
Malaysian palm oil futures declined by more than one percent on Wednesday, extending market losses into a second consecutive session. Ample supplies, sluggish destination demand, and downward pressure from competing edible oils contributed to the drop. At the market close, the benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange fell 49 ringgit, representing a 1.1% decrease to settle at 4,387 ringgit, or approximately $1,064.29, per metric ton.

Anilkumar Bagani, head of research at vegetable oil broker Sunvin Group, noted that the market experienced sharp drops as supply remained high while demand lagged. Bagani also highlighted that biodiesel premiums are diminishing alongside declining fossil fuel prices, making palm oil a less attractive feedstock option. Furthermore, a broad selloff across Chinese vegetable oil markets was largely driven by record-high domestic palm oil inventories.

Cargo surveyors reported that exports of Malaysian palm oil products for the first half of November dropped between 1% and 3.9% compared to the previous month. Concurrently, oil prices fell following an increase in United States crude and fuel inventories, though losses were partially mitigated by ongoing conflicts involving the US and Iran alongside vessel attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. In rival markets, Dalian's most-active soyoil contract dropped 1.56%, its palm oil contract fell 3.02%, and Chicago Board of Trade soyoil prices decreased by 1.58%. Meanwhile, the Malaysian ringgit weakened by 0.54% against the US dollar, offering minor relief to foreign currency holders.

stories.title: Pakistani Leadership Discusses Development and Reconstruction in Azad Jammu and Kashmir
stories.summary:
Top leadership of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) held a meeting in Muzaffarabad on Wednesday to discuss public welfare, development projects, and election promise implementation in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK). Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif met with AJK President Muhammad Najeeb Naqi Khan and Prime Minister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani to map out regional reconstruction efforts.

 पंजाब Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, along with federal and provincial ministers such as Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, also participated in the high-level discussions. During the gathering, both the federal and Punjab governments reaffirmed their commitment to supporting prosperity and development across the region.

The huddle follows the PML-N coming to power in AJK in August after phased elections. During the July election campaign, Nawaz Sharif had vowed to transform Muzaffarabad into a premier city in Pakistan, urging local leaders to emulate development models seen in Punjab. He had also pledged to visit every three months to ensure manifesto commitments were met and previously handed PM Gillani a 100-day reform agenda focusing on essential public services.

This regional engagement matters as the federal leadership attempts to fulfill campaign promises and extend basic rights like healthcare, education, sanitation, and reliable roads to remote areas of AJK rather than limiting them to major urban centers.

stories.title: SECP Significantly Reduces Nano-Loan Interest Rate Caps to Protect Borrowers
stories.summary:
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has substantially lowered the maximum costs that lenders can impose on digital nano-loans. Under newly issued Circular No. 26 of 2026, the annual percentage rate (APR) cap has been slashed from 274 percent down to 90 percent for new borrowers and 70 percent for repeat borrowers. These regulatory changes apply to unsecured digital loans up to Rs50,000 with maximum repayment terms of 90 days.

The updated framework aims to strengthen borrower safeguards and encourage responsible lending practices across mobile applications and digital wallets. The new limits equate to a maximum daily cost of about 0.2466 percent for new borrowers and 0.1918 percent for repeat borrowers, incorporating all associated mark-ups, processing fees, and platform charges. Furthermore, the regulation specifies that a repeat borrower is anyone who fully repays their latest loan to the same lender within the original period, which allows them to automatically benefit from the lower ceiling.

In addition to capping rates, the circular prohibits compounding, automatic rollovers, and hidden costs. Lenders must now permit early repayment with charges restricted only to the days the loan remained active, and they must provide a three-day grace period following the due date before imposing late-payment fees. Moreover, total recoveries, including principal, interest, and penalties, cannot exceed twice the original principal amount.

To further protect consumers, the SECP is currently developing a digital repository of nano-loan borrowers. This database will allow lenders to review existing obligations before approving additional credit, helping prevent over-indebtedness and encouraging cautious lending behavior if a borrower is already struggling to repay.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Finishes Session Flat Following Seven-Month High Amid Stronger Dollar
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee closed nearly flat on Wednesday, paring earlier gains after touching a seven-month peak during early trading. Robust foreign inflows into local equities provided initial tailwinds, but a broadly firmer US dollar ultimately eroded the currency's advances, leaving the rupee at 93.44 per dollar compared to its previous close of 93.47.

Earlier in the session, the currency reached an intra-day peak of 93.2550. However, the global dollar index climbed 0.2 percent to 103.8, hitting its highest level since April 2025. This strengthening greenback was driven by market expectations of faster interest rate increases by the US Federal Reserve, supported by positive economic data and hawkish statements from policymakers. Despite these dollar headwinds, the rupee has advanced approximately 1.5 percent over the month of November, bolstered by roughly $10 billion in foreign portfolio inflows.

Market participants noted that the rupee showed notable resilience despite the firmer dollar, aided by active exporters and positive non-deliverable forward market trends. According to DBS, the near-term outlook favors foreign exchange stability, though curbs implemented by the Reserve Bank of India remain in place. These central bank measures were initially introduced in October to limit dollar demand and protect the domestic currency from reaching record lows.

Later in the day, global financial markets shifted their primary focus toward Anthropic's share pricing ahead of its market debut. This frontier artificial intelligence firm's initial listing is viewed as a critical health check for the broader AI sector boom currently dominating global markets.

stories.title: Indian Equities Pull Back from Nine-Month Highs Driven by Profit-Taking
stories.summary:
Indian stock markets declined on Wednesday, undergoing consolidation after hitting near nine-month highs in the previous session. Benchmark indices Nifty 50 and Sensex dropped 0.63 percent and 0.61 percent, respectively, closing at 25,227.95 and 82,031.81. Thirteen out of sixteen major sectors registered losses, with broader small-cap and mid-cap indices falling by 0.4 percent and 1.2 percent.

Despite Wednesday's pullback, both major benchmarks have experienced substantial gains of roughly 9.4 percent and 10.2 percent over the course of November. This monthly surge was fueled by record foreign portfolio investor inflows totaling $10 billion, positive corporate earnings, easing oil prices, and the global AI-trade reversal following US midterm election results. Technical analysts noted that some profit-taking and consolidation at higher levels were natural after the recent rally pushed benchmarks into overbought territory.

Sector performance on Wednesday reflected broader macroeconomic pressures, notably a strengthening US dollar driven by anticipated US Federal Reserve rate hikes. The metal index dropped 2.5 percent due to lower global metal prices and currency pressures, while high-weightage financials fell 0.7 percent as investors locked in gains following a 14 percent monthly rise. Meanwhile, Brent crude futures declined 1.3 percent to $91.9 per barrel following data showing a rise in US crude and fuel inventories.

Individual stock movements varied based on corporate developments. IIFL Finance shares rose 4 percent after Canada's Fairfax exited the company through a $370 million block deal. Cipla gained 2.1 percent following a successful US regulatory clearance for its InvaGen Pharmaceuticals facility in New York, whereas Caplin Point dropped 7.2 percent after the US drug regulator urged corrective action at one of its units.

stories.title: پاکستان میں سولر توانائی کا انقلاب، بجلی کے بلوں سے پریشان عوام کا نیا سہارا
stories.summary:
پاکستان میں شمسی توانائی کے استعمال میں غیرمعمولی اضافہ دیکھا گیا ہے، جہاں اب سولر پینل دیہی علاقوں میں شادیوں کے تحائف سے لے کر گھروں کی چھتوں اور صنعتی کارخانوں تک عام ہو چکے ہیں۔ رینیوایبلز فرسٹ کے مطابق، 2018 سے 2025 کے درمیان ملک میں شمسی بجلی کا حصہ ایک فیصد سے بڑھ کر 28 فیصد ہو گیا ہے اور تقریباً 70 لاکھ گھرانوں میں سولر پینل نصب ہیں۔

اس رجحان کی بڑی وجہ بجلی کے دگنے نرخ اور طویل لوڈشیڈنگ ہے، جس کی وجہ سے اوسط ماہانہ آمدنی والے خاندان متبادل توانائی کی طرف مائل ہوئے ہیں۔ وزیرِ توانائی اویس احمد لغاری کے مطابق، لوگوں نے بڑھتے ہوئے اخراجات سے نمٹنے کے لیے خود متبادل راستہ اختیار کیا ہے، کیونکہ درآمدی چینی ساختہ سولر پینلز کی قیمتوں میں 93 فیصد کمی واقع ہوئی ہے۔

تاہم، ماہرین اس تیز رفتار منتقلی کے منفی اثرات سے بھی خبردار کرتے ہیں، جن میں ’یوٹیلٹی ڈیتھ سپائرل‘ کا خطرہ شامل ہے۔ قومی گرڈ پر باقی رہنے والے صارفین پر سالانہ 500 ملین ڈالر سے زیادہ کا اضافی بوجھ پڑ رہا ہے، کیونکہ زیادہ صارفین کے گرڈ سے ہٹنے کے اخراجات کم لوگوں پر پڑتے ہیں۔

حکومت کا ہدف ہے کہ 2036 تک ملک کی توانائی کا 90 فیصد حصہ صاف ذرائع سے حاصل ہو اور درآمدی ایندھن کا انحصار 4 فیصد تک لایا جائے۔ دریں اثنا، صنعتی ادارے جیسے راولپنڈی کی کوہِ نور ٹیکسٹائل ملز بھی پیداواری لاگت کم کرنے کے لیے سولر توانائی پر منتقل ہو رہی ہیں اور اب بیٹریاں نصب کر رہی ہیں۔

stories.title: Islamabad High Court Orders Medical Care and Hygienic Conditions for Bushra Bibi
stories.summary:
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) directed prison authorities to guarantee proper medical care and clean living conditions for Bushra Bibi. A division bench comprising Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif issued the directive while granting a seven-day adjournment for appeals filed by Bushra Bibi and her husband, PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan, against their convictions in the £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case. An accountability court in Islamabad had previously sentenced Imran to 14 years and Bushra to seven years in prison on January 17, 2025.

During the proceedings, Bushra's legal team, including Sardar Latif Khosa and Barrister Salman Safdar, raised serious health concerns through a fresh miscellaneous application. Khosa stated that Bushra required surgery due to deteriorating eyesight and potential complications, adding that her legal team had recently met with the couple at Adiala jail following prior court orders. The application also alleged that seven small snakes were found in her cell and killed by a prison official named Sibtain, heightening fears of infection if she undergoes surgery.

Justice Dogar assured the defense that the court had noted these concerns and would ensure Bushra receives all permitted facilities under prison rules while stating that the difficulties highlighted would not recur. The bench emphasized that health matters would be handled within its jurisdiction. Meanwhile, Barrister Safdar requested permission to broadcast the appeal proceedings live, noting previous high-profile broadcasts and public interest.

The case proceedings were attended by PTI leaders, defense lawyers, and prosecution officials, including National Accountability Bureau Prosecutor General Sohail Nasir and Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Hayat Malik. Strict security measures were deployed around the Islamabad High Court during the hearing.

stories.title: Nvidia Stops Shipping Hopper AI Chips to China Amid Regulatory Scrutiny
stories.summary:
Californian semiconductor firm Nvidia announced that it has ceased shipping artificial intelligence chips from its Hopper series to China. The decision arrives amid intensifying scrutiny regarding Beijing's access to powerful United States hardware, which remains critical for training and running advanced AI applications. During a recent earnings call, interim CEO Colette Kress stated that sales of licensed Hopper data centre products to China reached $2.4 billion in the third quarter, but current guidance excludes any such shipments.

While Kress did not provide an explicit reason for halting the shipments, market analysts suggest the move reflects Nvidia's efforts to clarify its business operations in China and prioritize regulatory compliance. Earlier, the Trump administration permitted limited sales of the flagship H200 chip from the Hopper lineup, though export restrictions continue to bar advanced GPUs like Blackwell and Rubin due to potential military applications. Additionally, trade complexities and domestic Chinese tech preferences have influenced market dynamics.

The halt coincides with broader US efforts to close loopholes in export controls. Washington recently introduced interim rules aimed at preventing chip smuggling and cracking down on gray markets where Chinese entities rent high-end computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia. These developments follow recent corporate controversies involving former executives and associated firms under investigation for helping Chinese companies bypass export restrictions.

Industry experts note that the practical impact of Nvidia halting Hopper shipments may be limited, as Chinese authorities have already encouraged domestic tech firms to look away from foreign chips like the H200 in favor of local alternatives. Analysts view the new US Commerce Department regulations restricting remote access to advanced computing capabilities as a far more consequential development in controlling technological decoupling.

stories.title: Counter Terrorism Department Foils Terror Plot in Okara and Arrests Suspect
stories.summary:
The Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) arrested a man accused of working for India's intelligence agency, Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), thereby thwarting an alleged terrorist plot in Okara. According to the First Information Report (FIR) registered by the CTD, the suspect was identified as Muhammad Syed Adnan Ali, a resident of Rawalpindi. He was taken into custody near the main gate of Palm City on Rao Sikandar Iqbal Road in Okara.

Law enforcement officials stated that the suspect was present in the area carrying explosive material to execute a terrorist attack. Authorities recovered an improvised explosive device (IED) weighing approximately 1,953 grams from his possession at the scene. The seized explosive device was reportedly rigged with a detonator, circuit, batteries, and wiring.

Following the recovery, the Bomb Disposal Squad was dispatched to the location and successfully defused the explosive device. A formal case has been registered against the arrested suspect by the authorities, and further investigations into the alleged plot and his network are currently underway.

stories.title: The Game Awards 2026 Announces Official Nominees for Twelfth Annual Ceremony
stories.summary:
The organizers of The Game Awards released the official list of nominees for their twelfth annual ceremony on November 17. The upcoming event will celebrate video games released throughout 2026 up until the cutoff date of November 20. This schedule allows highly anticipated titles, such as Grand Theft Auto VI, a strong possibility of earning multiple nominations, particularly since members of the event's jury gained access to the game starting in late October.

The twelfth annual Game Awards ceremony is scheduled to broadcast live on Thursday, December 10, from the Peacock Theatre in Los Angeles. As in previous years, the event will be hosted by Geoff Keighley. In addition to presenting awards across various competitive categories, the broadcast is anticipated to feature major video game news announcements.

stories.title: Saudi Weather Center Issues Red Alert for Makkah Heavy Rains
stories.summary:
Saudi Arabia’s National Center of Meteorology (NCM) has declared a high-priority red alert for severe rainfall driven by widespread thunderstorms sweeping across various territories of the Kingdom. Local officials are urging residents and visitors to exercise extreme caution throughout this active weather period.

The Makkah region experienced red alert conditions characterized by intense downpours, severe winds, zero horizontal visibility, lightning, hail, and flash flooding. Meanwhile, neighboring regions face orange alerts predicting moderate showers, high winds, and turbulent sea waves, particularly in parts of the Asir region.

Atmospheric instability continues to produce thundery precipitation accompanied by active winds and hail across portions of Jazan, Asir, Al Baha, and Makkah. Additionally, forecasters anticipate fog formations over these locations as well as specific areas within the Eastern Province.

These warnings underscore the importance of public vigilance as severe meteorological conditions impact multiple parts of the nation. Authorities remain on alert to manage potential hazards arising from the ongoing weather disruptions.

stories.title: Gold Prices in Pakistan Drop Below Rs400,000 Tola Milestone
stories.summary:
Gold values in Pakistan declined significantly on Wednesday, mirroring a downward trend in the international market. Local rates for gold per tola fell by Rs10,000 to reach Rs398,936, while 10 grams of gold decreased by Rs8,573 to sell at Rs342,023, according to figures released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA).

APGJSA representative Abdullah Chand noted that gold had previously crossed the Rs400,000 threshold following a market boom after September 27 of last year, marking a return to these lower price levels after nearly twelve months. Concurrently, international spot gold dropped by $100 to $3,764 per ounce, while domestic silver prices fell by Rs180 to settle at Rs5,048 per tola.

According to Kelvin Wong, senior market analyst at OANDA, the bearish market momentum stems from sentiment, technical factors, hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials, and climbing US Treasury yields that strengthened the US dollar. A steady dollar near a 19-month high made greenback-denominated bullion costlier for overseas buyers.

Adding to the pressure, Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams stated on Tuesday that the central bank may need to implement further rate hikes to counter inflation. Current market pricing via CME’s FedWatch tool indicates a 95.7 percent probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase in December, raising the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets.

stories.title: ABHI Microfinance Bank Public Subscription Reaches Rs547 Million Total
stories.summary:
ABHI Microfinance Bank Limited (AMFBL) successfully drew applications for 35,294,500 shares totaling Rs547.06 million against an issue size of 33,000,000 shares during its public subscription held on November 12 and 13. Arif Habib Limited reported to the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) that 6,080 applications were received, marking an oversubscription of roughly 1.07 times.

Under the allotment terms, requests for up to 2,000 shares will be fulfilled entirely, whereas applications exceeding 2,000 shares will receive allocations on a pro-rata basis. The bank aims to generate between Rs2 billion and Rs3 billion through an initial public offering (IPO) of 132 million ordinary shares on the PSX, utilizing a floor price of Rs15 per share.

Proceeds from the IPO are designed to alleviate capital shortages and drive the bank's Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) toward required regulatory levels. Management projects a net profit of around Rs1.5 billion for the second half of calendar year 2026, pushing the total projected profit for 2026 to approximately Rs3 billion, or specifically Rs2.927 billion according to forecasts.

With these earnings and IPO funds, the bank anticipates its CAR will reach approximately 4.3 percent by the close of 2026. Further profitability improvements in 2027 are expected to elevate the CAR to 17.8 percent, surpassing the State Bank of Pakistan's minimum threshold of 15 percent for microfinance institutions operating via branch-based and digital platforms across more than 108 cities.

stories.title: Cameron Bancroft Claims Entire Australian Team Knew Sandpaper Plot
stories.summary:
Former Australian cricketer Cameron Bancroft stated on Wednesday that the entire national squad was aware of the 2018 ball-tampering scheme in South Africa, directly contradicting statements made by current Test captain Pat Cummins. The controversy was recently reignited by Usman Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr, which claimed collective team knowledge and received strong backing from teammate David Warner.

A prior Cricket Australia investigation concluded that only then-captain Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner, and Bancroft bore responsibility for utilizing sandpaper to alter the ball during the third Test in Cape Town, leading to their dismissal and subsequent bans. Cummins asserted publicly last Friday that Khawaja was completely incorrect regarding the team's widespread involvement.

Breaking his silence in a column for the West Australian, Bancroft admitted he withheld vital details during the initial investigation, including the duration of the ball-tampering and the awareness of other players, in order to protect Cricket Australia's inquiry. He explained that Khawaja's book and Cummins' repeated denials compelled him to reveal the truth to relieve a long-carried personal burden.

Bancroft expressed feelings of anger, betrayal, and isolation regarding Cummins' public account of the tour. While Cricket Australia has ruled out launching a new probe into the incident, the latest disclosures have intensified ongoing debates within the sport surrounding the 2018 scandal.

stories.title: Prince William and Kate Middleton Conclude India Trip in Mumbai
stories.summary:
Britain's Prince William and his wife, Kate Middleton, concluded their three-day visit to India's financial capital, Mumbai, with separate engagements before heading to New Delhi to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Prince William spent part of his Wednesday touring Dharma Productions, a prominent Bollywood studio in suburban Mumbai. During his visit, he watched dancers perform to a track from the hit movie "Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham" and met with filmmakers and actors, including Karan Johar, Saif Ali Khan, and Kareena Kapoor.

Simultaneously, the Princess of Wales visited a maternity hospital in central Mumbai to speak with health workers. This overseas tour marked a high-profile appearance for the princess following her cancer treatment in 2024. Earlier during their whirlwind stay in the city of 13 million people, the royal couple participated in various activities, such as playing cricket with retired player Sachin Tendulkar, touring a craft school, and attending the Earthshot Prize awards ceremony.

The climate-change awards, established by Prince William six years ago, featured Kate presenting an award in a bright red Indian-style gown. During the ceremony, Prince William delivered a speech highlighting the growing threats of global warming, pointing to frequent heatwaves and severe floods as a critical warning for the planet. The royal visit heavily emphasized cultural exchange and environmental action across its itinerary.

The concluding events in Mumbai successfully bridged international diplomacy with local cultural appreciation, showcasing Indian cinema and healthcare efforts. The royal couple's final meeting with Prime Minister Modi in New Delhi was scheduled for Wednesday evening, marking the official end of their busy diplomatic tour in the region.

stories.title: Cameron Bancroft Claims Entire Australian Cricket Team Knew About Sandpaper Plot
stories.summary:
Former Australian cricketer Cameron Bancroft has stated that the entire national team was aware of the 2018 ball-tampering plot during the South African tour, directly challenging assertions made by current captain Pat Cummins. The controversy, widely known as "Sandpapergate," previously led to a Cricket Australia investigation which concluded that only captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner, and Bancroft were accountable for utilizing sandpaper on the ball during the third Test in Cape Town. All three players were sent home and given suspensions.

The debate recently resurfaced following claims in Usman Khawaja's autobiography, "Sabr," which alleged collective team awareness. David Warner strongly supported Khawaja's statement, while Pat Cummins firmly denied the accusations during a press conference, calling them entirely incorrect. Breaking his silence on the matter, Bancroft wrote a column for the West Australian newspaper revealing that many others on the tour knew about his actions on the field.

Bancroft admitted that he withheld crucial details during the initial Cricket Australia probe, including the timeline of the sandpaper use and the extent of other team members' awareness, in order to protect the investigation and shield those around him. He noted that the release of Khawaja's book helped bring those memories back and offered a sense of personal relief regarding the true sequence of events.

However, Bancroft stated that Cummins' public denials were the final catalyst for him to speak out publicly. He expressed feelings of anger, betrayal, and isolation, noting that the public narrative maintained by Cummins did not align with what actually occurred and was experienced by everyone on that specific tour in South Africa.

stories.title: Pakistan Receives Record 15,000-Tonne LPG Shipment at Port Qasim
stories.summary:
Pakistan has taken delivery of the largest liquefied petroleum gas shipment in its national history, with a cargo of 15,000 metric tonnes arriving at Port Qasim. The shipment has been successfully berthed at the Engro Vopak Terminal as part of ongoing government initiatives to restructure and reform the country's LPG sector.
