Board Chairman Harvey Jones announced the decision during a conference call with investors, stating that the company has retained the executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles. Jones emphasized that while the board aims to install a permanent leader quickly, they will prioritize finding the right candidate over expediting the process.

The leadership transition comes amid high financial stakes for the world's most valuable chipmaker, which recently reported a more than doubled third-quarter revenue of $115.84 billion, beating analysts' expectations of $109.11 billion. Interim CEO and finance chief Colette Kress, along with vice president Ian Buck and Chairman Jones, addressed financial and technical questions on the call. Kress reported strong operational support from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co and noted an explosive start for the company's newest flagship AI processor, Vera Rubin. Nvidia forecasted fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, surpassing Wall Street's average estimate of $125.25 billion.

Huang's departure followed revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, which has prompted inquiries from US intelligence agencies regarding her potential ties to China's Ministry of State Security. Additionally, the Wall Street Journal reported that the US Securities and Exchange Commission has launched a probe into Nvidia following the resignation. Despite these complications and a campaign to reinstate Huang—who stated he would be honored to return if deemed best by the board—analysts noted that Nvidia's established executive team provides near-term stability while the company navigates complex national security and export control scrutiny.

Market reactions to the company's performance and leadership update included a 4% rise in extended trading shares, though Nvidia's market value remains down about $2 trillion from its early October high. Investors continue to monitor broader risks, including potential regulatory impacts from a Democratic sweep in US midterm elections and ongoing debates over AI infrastructure spending. Meanwhile, predictions for Huang's permanent successor include internal and external candidates, with industry figures like Arm CEO Rene Haas and Nvidia's Ian Buck frequently mentioned by market observers.

stories.title: Apple Restores Services After Internal Update Triggers Outage for iCloud and Apple Pay
stories.summary:
Apple Inc. announced on Tuesday that it was actively working to restore its digital systems following an internal update that caused a service outage affecting customer platforms such as iCloud and Apple Pay. The technology giant confirmed that the disruption was not the result of a cyberattack and stated that many of its systems were already functioning again. A company spokesperson assured the public that efforts were underway to bring the remaining offline systems back online as quickly as possible.

The outage led to significant user activity on tracking platforms, with Downdetector recording approximately 2,300 user reports of issues concerning Apple Pay in the United States around 12:20 pm Eastern Time. At the peak of the disruption, the tracking platform also logged roughly 1,800 user-submitted problem reports regarding iCloud services. While these figures are based on user status reports and actual affected user numbers may vary, the incident drew widespread attention from consumers attempting to access digital wallets and cloud storage.

This technical disruption at Apple coincides with a recent wave of high-profile technology failures across the United States. Previous days saw incidents including a global Microsoft outage, a Federal Aviation Administration network failure that triggered a nationwide ground stop, a United Airlines technical failure, and a JPMorgan Chase software problem that impacted select banking operations. Similar to Apple's situation, relevant companies and officials confirmed that these preceding technology disruptions were also unrelated to cyberattacks.

The temporary outage highlights the growing operational vulnerabilities of major cloud and payment ecosystems as firms routinely push internal system updates. Apple continues to monitor its infrastructure to ensure full functionality is restored across all affected services globally. Users relying on iCloud for data synchronization and Apple Pay for transactions experienced brief interruptions before core operations began recovering.

stories.title: Indian Shares Anticipate Lower Open Following Recent Rally and Record Foreign Inflows
stories.summary:
Indian benchmark indices are projected to open lower on Wednesday as investors pause for consolidation following a sharp market rally. GIFT Nifty futures indicated a negative start for the Nifty 50 index at 25,253 points, following a previous close of 25,387.4. Analysts note that some market consolidation is warranted after a 13% surge over just 12 trading sessions. Despite the expected pullback, easing crude oil prices and robust foreign fund inflows are anticipated to limit potential losses for the broader market.

Foreign portfolio investors have driven strong momentum in November, pushing the Nifty and BSE Sensex up by 10.1% and 10.8% respectively. FPI inflows reached a record $10 billion for the month, supported by 12 consecutive sessions of net buying. Provisional data showed that foreign investors purchased Indian shares worth 41.95 billion rupees, equivalent to $448.81 million, during the previous session alone. This strong domestic liquidity has helped cushion Indian equities against broader regional market fluctuations.

In the broader Asian region, market sentiment received a boost as MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan advanced 0.9%. This recovery followed a four-day losing streak, aided by Nvidia's stronger-than-expected sales forecast that lifted companies across its hardware supply chain. Meanwhile, energy markets saw Brent crude futures fall 0.5% to $92.7 per barrel, bringing the contract down 21% for the month as traders weighed Middle East export recovery against ongoing tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.

In corporate and regulatory developments within India, exchange operators and brokerage shares remain in focus following reports that authorities may limit leveraged stock bets to curb market volatility. Brokerage firm Jefferies indicated that this policy proposal poses limited risk, as firms have already reduced exposure to less liquid equities. Additionally, IIFL Finance shares will draw attention amid reports that Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings plans to divest its nearly 11% stake in the non-bank lender to finance its acquisition of a 60% stake in IDBI Bank.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Outperforms Asian Currencies Amid Strong Foreign Inflows
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee is expected to extend its strong performance relative to other Asian currencies, supported by favorable oil prices and a major revival in foreign equity inflows. Following a rally that pushed the currency to a more than seven-month high, it settled at 93.47 against the dollar and crossed the critical 93.60 technical barrier.

Bankers and market participants note that this breakthrough could clear the path for further appreciation if the Reserve Bank of India permits it. Overseas investors have injected nearly $10 billion into Indian equities during the month, which has helped offset regional market weaknesses and coincided with a cooling of the artificial intelligence investment trade.

The influx of capital provides the Reserve Bank of India an opportunity to acquire dollars, helping to rebuild foreign exchange reserves and effectively manage a near $240 billion dollar forward book. Currency traders indicate that market momentum firmly favors the rupee as US equities extend their losses and portfolio flows continue shifting toward India.

stories.title: Asian Markets Rebound as Nvidia Forecast Softens Tech Sector Losses
stories.summary:
Stocks across Asia advanced as chipmaker Nvidia delivered a stronger-than-expected sales forecast that helped the regional benchmark recover from four consecutive sessions of losses. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan gained 0.9%, while South Korea’s KOSPI climbed up to 3.3% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 0.6%.

The positive market movement followed Nvidia reporting quarterly revenue above forecasts in its first earnings report since Jensen Huang’s departure as CEO, sending its shares up 4.7% in after-hours trading. This performance offered a crucial indicator for the artificial intelligence hardware supply chain, overshadowing a Wall Street Journal report concerning a Securities and Exchange Commission probe into the company.

Investor attention now turns toward Anthropic's upcoming market debut, which could value the firm at up to $1.4 trillion. Meanwhile, economic data showed Japan's exports grew for the 14th consecutive month in October, and US economic indicators revealed rising Treasury yields alongside Federal Reserve commentary regarding potential interest rate hikes to curb inflation.

stories.title: Oil Prices Slip as Rising US Crude Inventories Offset Middle East Risks
stories.summary:
Crude oil prices declined due to data indicating a substantial increase in US crude and fuel inventories during the previous week. West Texas Intermediate futures decreased by 56 cents to $85.45 a barrel, while Brent crude futures dropped 16 cents to $92.98 a barrel following reports from the American Petroleum Institute.

The American Petroleum Institute data revealed that US crude stocks grew by 5.28 million barrels in the week ending November 13, alongside a 5.12 million barrel increase in gasoline stocks and a 351,000 barrel rise in distillates. However, broader declines were kept in check by escalating geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran, as well as ongoing maritime navigation threats in the Strait of Hormuz.

Supply concerns persisted after Bahrain reported intercepting Iranian aerial attacks targeting the country, which hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet. These incidents followed mutual strikes between the US and Iran, a projectile strike on an LPG tanker near Oman, and Houthi drone launches targeting pumping stations along Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline.

stories.title: Pakistani Man Sentenced to Over 27 Years for US Political Assassination Plot
stories.summary:
A federal judge in Brooklyn sentenced 48-year-old Pakistani national Asif Merchant to 330 months in prison for attempting to commit an act of terrorism transcending national boundaries and murder for hire. The Department of Justice confirmed the sentence following a trial that established Merchant traveled to the United States to arrange political assassinations.

Federal prosecutors stated that Merchant attempted to recruit individuals within the US to target Donald Trump, Joe Biden, and Nikki Haley as retaliation for the 2020 assassination of Iranian military commander Qassem Soleimani. Law enforcement intervened before any attacks could occur after an individual Merchant contacted in April 2024 reported the scheme and became a confidential informant.

During his trial, Merchant testified that he participated in the plot under duress from Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to protect his family in Tehran, though a federal jury ultimately convicted him in March. Tehran has consistently denied any involvement in plotting attacks against American officials, amid a backdrop of broader ongoing military conflicts involving the US, Israel, and Iran.

stories.title: امریکہ میں ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ کے قتل کی سازش پر پاکستانی شہری کو سزا
stories.summary: امریکہ کی ایک وفاقی عدالت نے پاکستان سے تعلق رکھنے والے اٹھارہ سالہ آصف مرچنٹ کو تیرہ ماہ قید کی سزا سنا دی ہے۔ بروکلین میں امریکی ڈسٹرکٹ جج ایرک آر کومیٹی نے آصف مرچنٹ کو سرحدی دہشت گردی کی کوشش اور معاوضے کے قتل کی سازش کے الزامات میں مجرم قرار دیا۔ مارچ دو ہزار چھبیس میں وفاقی جیوری نے انہیں ان الزامات میں قصوروار ٹھہرایا تھا۔ محکمہ انصاف کے مطابق ملزم نے اعتراف کیا کہ وہ پاسداران انقلاب سے وابستہ تھے اور امریکی حکام کے قتل کی منصوبہ بندی کے لیے امریکہ آئے۔ استغاثہ کا کہنا تھا کہ اس سازش کا بنیادی ہدف ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ تھے، جبکہ سابق صدر جو بائیڈن اور سابق سفیر نکی ہیلی بھی ممکنہ اہداف میں شامل ہو سکتے تھے۔ عدالتی دستاویزات کے مطابق مرچنٹ نے بتایا کہ انہیں دو ہزار بیس کے قریب بھرتی کیا گیا، جس کے بعد انہوں نے تہران کے دورے کیے اور رابطہ افسر سے ملاقاتیں کیں۔ تہران ان الزامات کی تردید کرتا ہے۔ محکمہ انصاف کا الزام ہے کہ اس منصوبے کا مقصد ایرانی کمانڈر قاسم سلیمانی کے قتل کا بدلہ لینا تھا جو جنوری دو ہزار بیس میں بغداد میں ایک ڈرون حملے میں مارے گئے تھے۔ آصف مرچنٹ اپریل دو ہزار چوبیس میں امریکہ پہنچے اور ایک شخص سے رابطہ کیا جس نے ایف بی آئی کو اطلاع دے دی اور مخبر بن گیا۔ بعد میں مرچنٹ نے ایف بی آئی کے خفیہ اہلکاروں سے رابطہ کیا اور پانچ ہزار ڈالر کی ابتدائی ادائیگی کی۔ جولائی دو ہزار چوبیس میں انہیں ٹیکساس کے شہر رچمنڈ سے اس وقت گرفتار کیا گیا جب وہ امریکہ چھوڑنے کی تیاری کر رہے تھے۔ مقدمے کی سماعت کے دوران مرچنٹ نے بتایا کہ وہ کیلا برآمد کرنے اور گارمنٹس کے کاروبار سے وابستہ رہے ہیں، اور ان کے اہل خانہ دباؤ میں تھے۔ سزا کے بعد امریکی اٹارنی جنرل اور ایف بی آئی حکام نے اس فیصلے کا خیرمقدم کیا۔

stories.title: MQM-P Calls for Nationwide Referendum on New Provinces Ahead of 2027
stories.summary:
The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) has urged the government to hold a nationwide referendum in December under Article 48(6) of the Constitution to let citizens decide on creating new administrative units. Speaking at a press conference at the party’s Bahadurabad headquarters in Karachi on Tuesday, senior leader Dr Farooq Sattar also demanded that Article 140-A be properly incorporated into the proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment to ensure the devolution of power to local governments. Dr Sattar argued that public opinion must dictate whether additional provinces are formed, criticizing political leaders who stand in the way of this democratic right.

Later, the party strongly condemned PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s recent warning that carving up Sindh would lead to bloodshed. The MQM-P questioned why creating provinces across the country would trigger violence exclusively in urban areas of Sindh, asserting that the majority of urban residents support new administrative units. The party also addressed the plight of over 5,000 federal government quarters facing eviction in Karachi, warning that thousands of families risk homelessness. Dr Sattar noted that these quarters house descendants of migrants invited by Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah, who have lived there for decades.

Highlighting the historical context, Dr Sattar stated that former leaders Zulfikar Ali Bhutto in 1972, General Ziaul Haq in 1979, and the Supreme Court in a 1984 judgment had protected residents from eviction. He added that subsequent administrations, including those of Benazir Bhutto and Nawaz Sharif, reaffirmed ownership rights, while a 2019 Supreme Court order directed that the issue be resolved through local stakeholders and elected officials. Dr Sattar accused Karachi Estate Office officials of misapplying 2002 rental rules and wrongfully deducting funds from retired employees' pensions. He warned that the MQM-P would surround the Estate Office if eviction notices were not halted, emphasizing that the party would stand by the affected families.

stories.title: LUMS National AI Hub Signs Deal to Support Public-Sector Healthcare
stories.summary:
The National AI Hub for Maternal, Newborn and Child Health (MNCH) at the Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Office of Artificial Intelligence Punjab. The agreement aims to introduce responsible artificial intelligence tools into public-sector healthcare across the province. By connecting Punjab's AI agenda with LUMS research expertise, the partnership focuses on creating practical, evidence-informed tools to assist healthcare providers and strengthen health-system decision-making.

The official signing ceremony took place in the presence of several key officials. Attendees included Health Minister Khawaja Imran Nazir, Ali Dar, adviser to the Chief Minister on AI, Office of AI Punjab Secretary Ahmad Rajwana, LUMS Acting Vice Chancellor Dr. Tariq Jadoon, and Hub Director Dr. Maryam Mustafa. Additionally, a visiting delegation from the Gates Foundation, featuring Dr. Anita Zaidi and Dr. Kalpana Kochhar, toured the Hub to review its ongoing initiatives and explore potential collaborations for improving health outcomes and equitable access to medical care.

Beyond this provincial agreement, the LUMS Hub has previously established partnerships with the Government of Sindh and the Aga Khan University. Through these collaborations, the institutions are working on developing clinical decision-support systems, AI-based risk-stratification models, and voice-assisted tools specifically designed to aid frontline maternal and child healthcare workers in their daily duties.

stories.title: Pakistan and Portugal to Host Joint Business Forum in Islamabad
stories.summary:
Pakistan and Portugal are scheduled to hold a Business Forum in Islamabad on November 23, 2026, aimed at boosting bilateral trade, investment, and business matchmaking. The event coincides with the official visit of Portugal’s Minister of Foreign Affairs to Pakistan. To organize the forum, the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) has established a Joint Working Group (JWG) in collaboration with the Portuguese Embassy in Islamabad, which expects a visiting delegation of Portuguese businesses to attend.

The forum will focus on key economic sectors identified for potential partnerships, including agriculture and agri-food, energy, pharmaceuticals, information technology, textiles, sports goods, and surgical instruments. To facilitate direct interactions, the SIFC has instructed various government ministries to identify seven to ten leading companies within their respective domains and submit comprehensive details regarding their business interests and export potentials in Portugal.

The organizing framework is led by a Joint Working Group chaired by Ambassador Abrar H. Hashmi, Additional Secretary for SIFC and Economic Diplomacy at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, alongside Co-Chairperson Dr. Erfa Iqbal, Additional Secretary of SIFC. The group has been granted the authority to co-opt additional members to ensure the successful execution of the forum and foster stronger commercial ties between the two nations.

stories.title: Pakistan Army Chief and Iranian Foreign Minister Discuss Regional Security
stories.summary:
Pakistan and Iran have emphasized the necessity of maintaining ongoing dialogue, building mutual trust, and enhancing coordination to tackle shared security challenges and foster regional stability. This consensus was reached during a meeting in Rawalpindi on Monday between Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces (COAS & CDF), and a visiting high-level Iranian delegation headed by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

According to an Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) statement issued on Tuesday, the discussions covered topics of mutual interest, regional security dynamics, and geopolitical shifts, alongside exploring methods to address common security concerns. Field Marshal Asim Munir highlighted that sustained bilateral engagement and close cooperation between the neighboring countries are vital for ensuring lasting peace and stability in the region.

In response, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi praised Pakistan for its constructive contributions toward regional peace and expressed Tehran's commitment to deepening bilateral ties. The meeting underscored the shared priority both nations place on continued communication and collaborative efforts to navigate complex security environments in the region.

stories.title: Ufone and Tenedor Partner with AlfaMall for 5G Phone Financing
stories.summary:
Pakistani telecommunications companies Ufone and Tenedor Pakistan have officially entered into a strategic collaboration with AlfaMall, which is operated by Bank Alfalah as a leading Buy Now, Pay Later marketplace in the country. The agreement was finalized in Islamabad during a formal ceremony by Badar Bin Saqib, who serves as the Vice President of Segments and Products for PTML, and Ms. Robina Naz, the Regional Head of Corporate North for AlfaMall.

The primary objective of this new alliance is to make fifth-generation smartphones far more accessible and financially manageable for consumers through structured installment financing programs. Because the high cost of compatible mobile devices has traditionally acted as a major obstacle preventing the broader adoption of advanced network technology locally, this initiative seeks to bridge that gap by offering customers flexible payment alternatives.

Under the terms of the arrangement, eligible buyers will be able to purchase modern 5G handsets utilizing credit cards issued directly by Bank Alfalah alongside other participating financial institutions, thereby eliminating the burden of paying the full retail price upfront. Company executives believe that this measure will successfully encourage everyday users to upgrade their hardware while simultaneously strengthening the overall digital ecosystem and expanding national connectivity.

Syed Atif Raza, the Chief Commercial Officer of PTML, emphasized that democratizing next-generation technology remains a core priority for the organization across various income brackets. Meanwhile, Ms. Robina Naz noted that the project highlights AlfaMall's dedication to providing innovative financial instruments while supporting the expansion of the broader digital economy within Pakistan.

stories.title: SMEDA and Alibaba.com Set Grant Program Launch for November 19
stories.summary:
The Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority together with Alibaba.com will unveil a specialized financial grant program on November 19 to help local enterprises adopt digital business tools and gain access to global markets. This upcoming launch coincides with the 100-day milestone of their joint digital export initiative and will be hosted at the Hannover Event Complex during the grand finale of the Pakistan AI Export Voice 2026 conference.

Officials confirmed that the gathering will unite diverse industry participants, including manufacturers, trade representatives, and small business owners. Furthermore, the ceremony will feature the announcement of the Grand Champion of the initiative alongside Pakistan's top three artificial intelligence cross-border ambassadors, with SMEDA Chief Executive Officer Nadia Jahangir Seth participating on the event's evaluation jury.

This cooperative effort stems from a memorandum of understanding originally established in May 2026 during Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's official visit to China. The overarching partnership is designed to train roughly 10,000 micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises while onboarding up to 2,000 qualified local businesses onto the digital marketplace managed by Alibaba.com through specialized technical guidance and preferential pricing structures.

Under the newly introduced grant scheme, qualified enterprises can obtain reimbursement-based monetary support reaching up to Rs150,000 subject to specific regulatory guidelines. Initial priority areas slated to receive this targeted assistance include agricultural machinery, auto parts, textiles, and sports goods and sportswear.

stories.title: Punjab Minister Reviews Housing Progress as Thousands of Homes Completed
stories.summary:
Provincial Minister for Housing Punjab Bilal Yasin led the 111th governing body session of the Punjab Housing and Town Planning Agency in Lahore. The gathering evaluated administrative updates, general performance, and proposed modifications to existing rules, including updates to the World Bank-backed affordable housing initiative designed to streamline project execution safely and transparently.

Officials reported that over 129,000 homes have been finalized through the Apni Chhat Apna Ghar Programme, while building efforts continue on an additional 63,843 residences. Director General Sikandar Zeeshan updated the participants regarding upcoming arrangements for an event scheduled in Multan later in the month.

Minister Bilal Yasin instructed that all preparations be finalized comprehensively within the designated timeline. He further ordered the priority distribution of second portions of interest-free loans to eligible beneficiary families to quicken construction progress.

Additionally, the Minister revealed that Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif will interact with program beneficiaries during her scheduled trip to Multan during the month. He emphasized that the interest-free financial assistance has brought substantial relief to thousands of households, highlighting official dedication to ensuring accessible and dignified homeownership for ordinary citizens.

stories.title: FBR Authorizes Seven New Vendors for Digital Beverage Monitoring
stories.summary:
The Federal Board of Revenue has officially cleared seven additional commercial entities to supply, install, and maintain electronic production monitoring systems across the domestic beverage industry. This update broadens the roster of approved service providers within the official digital monitoring framework.

Under this directive, more than 54 beverage businesses will be mandated to integrate production monitoring technology from certified suppliers. The updated roster encompasses various sub-sectors within the beverage industry, including bottled water, packaged juices, packaged milk, and carbonated waters or beverages.

This administrative addendum follows previous general orders issued between mid-May and early June 2026, operating under specific provisions of the Sales Tax Act of 1990 and associated sales tax rules. The newly approved service providers include the National Radio and Telecommunication Corporation, Obsidian Technologies, Excellence Delivered (Pvt.) Ltd., ISSM Labelling Solutions (Pvt.) Ltd., Tollink Pakistan (Private) Limited, AJCL (Pvt.) Ltd., and Authentik.

The revenue authority has instructed all designated vendors to guarantee that their technological setups fully adhere to regulatory requirements outlined in the relevant sales tax directives. Furthermore, registered entities governed by earlier orders are permitted to select any authorized supplier, including these newly added firms, to complete their system installations.

stories.title: Pakistan and UK Military Chiefs Discuss Enhanced Defence Cooperation
stories.summary:
Pakistan and the United Kingdom have renewed their dedication to deepening bilateral defense and security ties, placing special emphasis on expanding military-to-military engagement amid changing regional security dynamics. This consensus emerged during formal discussions held at the General Headquarters in Rawalpindi.

The talks took place between Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, and a visiting senior British delegation headed by General Sir Charles Roland Vincent Walker, Chief of the General Staff of the British Army. Representatives from both nations evaluated mutual interests, the current regional security climate, and potential pathways for broader collaboration.

Both sides expressed contentment regarding the enduring and friendly diplomatic history shared between Pakistan and the United Kingdom, reaffirming their commitment to reinforce military partnerships. Field Marshal Asim Munir highlighted Pakistan's strong resolve to widen defense connections with British counterparts during the dialogue.

In response, General Sir Charles Walker praised the operational readiness and professionalism of the Pakistan Armed Forces, acknowledging their ongoing contributions toward regional stability and peace. Upon his arrival at the military headquarters, the British Army commander was received with a Guard of Honour by a local army contingent, underscoring the mutual desire of both nations to solidify bilateral military bonds.

stories.title: Power Consumers Face Extra Cost Burden for July-September Quarter
stories.summary:
Electricity consumers across distribution company jurisdictions and K-Electric face an impending financial surcharge of roughly Rs1.34 per unit for the third quarter of 2026. Authorities intend to recover approximately Rs24 billion over a three-month span covering December 2026, January 2027, and February 2027.

The proposed tariff adjustment stems from a significant drop in Maximum Demand Indicator levels, a transition in cost allocation methodologies, and reduced revenue recovery tied to subsidized electricity supplied to industrial and agricultural users under a specific consumption package. The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority hosted a public hearing to review the quarterly tariff adjustments, overseen by board members Amina Ahmed, Maqsood Anwar Khan, and Ghulamullah Shaikh.

During the proceedings, aggregate claims submitted by distribution companies totaled Rs23.908 billion against baseline assumptions, driven heavily by capacity charges, variable operation and maintenance costs, and transmission loss impacts. Conversely, negative adjustments linked to incremental consumption offset a large portion of these positive claims, resulting in a net adjustment requirement of around Rs23.989 billion distributed unevenly across various regional utility companies.

Industry representatives and consumer advocates raised concerns during the public session regarding the financial impact on industrial sectors and questioned the accounting methodologies used to calculate incremental consumption and network charges. Critics argued that the current treatment of subsidized package units increases overall consumer claims rather than reducing them, prompting detailed regulatory scrutiny into specific operational fees and transmission infrastructure constraints.

stories.title: World Bank Warns Pakistan Faces High Financial Sector Vulnerabilities
stories.summary:
The World Bank has placed Pakistan among the countries experiencing elevated financial sector risks. This warning was issued on Tuesday as part of the organization's Finance and Prosperity 2026 report. The assessment highlights vulnerabilities stemming from heavy reliance on domestic banks to fulfill government financing requirements, along with macro-fiscal imbalances and shallow financial markets.

According to the report, Pakistan, Egypt, and Tunisia continue depending heavily on local banks to address pressing public sector needs. The World Bank cautions that holding large amounts of fragile sovereign debt creates significant financial stability risks, particularly for nations with limited capacity to handle such pressures. Furthermore, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have amplified global uncertainty, driven up commodity prices, tightened financial conditions, and increased market volatility.

The publication also drew attention to challenges facing micro, small, and medium enterprises, noting a global financing gap of USD 4 trillion across developing countries between 2019 and 2023. While these smaller businesses represent 90 percent of enterprises and 75 percent of employment in emerging economies, they face major credit hurdles. Access to formal loans can boost enterprise employment by an average of 12 percent and raise sales and profits by about 18 percent.

Additionally, the report pointed out that natural disaster insurance remains a major financial vulnerability. Uninsured financial losses exceeded 80 percent over the past decade in parts of Africa, Asia, and Latin America. The World Bank recommends that developing economies strengthen prudential supervision, improve safety nets, reduce disaster risks, and enhance insurance affordability to tackle these intertwined macro-fiscal, climate, and structural challenges.

stories.title: Asian Development Bank Approves USD 500 Million Pension Loan
stories.summary:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved a USD 500 million results-based loan dedicated to helping Pakistan reform its federal civil pension system. Announced via an official statement, the financing aims to contain surging pension fiscal pressures, ensure long-term system sustainability, and expand fiscal space for vital social and development spending.

Federal pension expenditures in Pakistan have increased nearly fivefold since fiscal year 2016, currently surpassing Rs 1 trillion annually. The traditional legacy defined benefit scheme is entirely unfunded, noncontributory, and financed through yearly budget allocations, generating continuous fiscal strain. Emma Fan, the ADB Country Director for Pakistan, noted that the programme will support and institutionalize ongoing federal efforts to build a more transparent and sustainable system.

The funds will back the initial phase of the government's Pension Reform Implementation Plan. A key component of this transition is the adoption of a defined contribution pension scheme, which has become mandatory for federal civil employees appointed starting in July 2024. ADB's backing is intended to help reduce liabilities, improve digital financial transparency, and enhance both service delivery and financial literacy among beneficiaries.

The broader programme centers on three primary outputs designed to establish a comprehensive reform model. These include institutionalizing a sustainable pension framework, enhancing the operational oversight of the defined contribution pension scheme, and establishing a sustainable training and awareness framework for the new system.

stories.title: Prime Minister Sharif Asks Endeavor Group to Aid Start-ups
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with a delegation from the global non-profit Endeavor Group in Islamabad on Tuesday. During the meeting, he urged the organization to broaden its support for Pakistani entrepreneurs by helping start-ups develop business capabilities, secure international mentorship, and connect with global investors and markets.

Sharif emphasized that Pakistan's young population holds immense entrepreneurial potential. He stated that the government is actively building an environment where emerging businesses can thrive internationally, noting that technology, innovation, and entrepreneurship are vital drivers of economic growth. The prime minister also pointed to the recent inauguration of an Information Technology Park in Islamabad, designed to serve as a modern technology ecosystem through close collaboration between universities and industry.

The Endeavor delegation briefed Sharif on their international initiatives and local operations. Operating in Pakistan since 2022, the organization provides guidance and consultancy to high-impact entrepreneurs. Through a comprehensive selection process, Endeavor has chosen eight Pakistani start-ups to receive mentorship and various forms of support.

Several high-ranking government officials attended the discussion. The attendees included federal ministers Ahsan Iqbal, Ahad Cheema, Attaullah Tarar, and Shaza Fatima, alongside other senior officials.

stories.title: Pakistan Posts First Current Account Surplus of Fiscal Year
stories.summary:
Pakistan recorded a current account surplus of USD 39 million in October 2026, breaking a four-month deficit streak and marking the first surplus of FY27. The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) reported this positive figure on Tuesday, contrasting sharply with deficits of USD 371 million in September 2026 and USD 307 million in October 2025.

Analysts noted that the October surplus was primarily fueled by a reduced import bill and an 8 percent month-on-month increase in home remittances. Specifically, the country's import bill decreased from USD 6.16 billion in September to USD 5.87 billion in October. Cumulatively, the current account deficit for the first four months of FY27 dropped by 20 percent to USD 850 million, compared to USD 1.062 billion during the same period in FY26.

During the July-October period of FY27, the trade deficit widened by 17 percent year-on-year to USD 12.3 billion, while workers' remittances grew by 14 percent year-on-year to reach USD 14.8 billion. Despite ongoing economic activity and elevated global commodity prices, the SBP projects the full-year current account deficit for FY27 to remain between 0 and 1.0 percent of GDP, helped by resilient goods and services exports alongside steady remittance inflows.

This follows a strong performance in the previous fiscal year. During FY26, the current account recorded a marginal deficit of just 0.1 percent of GDP, as rising remittances and ICT service exports offset higher imports and lower goods exports. SBP foreign exchange reserves successfully surpassed the USD 18 billion target by the end of June 2026, supported by the contained current account deficit, international capital market access, and multilateral and bilateral inflows.

stories.title: Pakistan Foreign Economic Assistance Surges Threefold in First Quarter
stories.summary:
Pakistan experienced a threefold rise in foreign economic assistance, securing USD 5.445 billion during the initial quarter of the 2026-27 fiscal year compared to USD 1.815 billion in the same period of the previous year. This substantial increase was detailed in figures published by the Economic Affairs Division (EAD) on Tuesday, highlighting an expanded reliance on external financing between July and September.

The majority of the total assistance, specifically USD 4.2 billion, was delivered as budgetary support, accompanied by USD 111.63 million in programme loans and USD 238.44 million from short-term Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) financing. Non-project loans accounted for USD 4.541 billion, while project loans received an allocation of USD 907.71 million. September alone recorded multilateral and bilateral loans and grants totaling USD 952.26 million.

Bilateral contributions during the July-September period included funds from Germany, France, Saudi Arabia, Korea, Denmark, Japan, the United States, and China. Concurrently, multilateral support arrived from institutions such as the Asian Development Bank (ADB), Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), International Development Association (IDA), IsDB, International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), and the OPEC Fund for International Development.

Additional inflows featured USD 300 million in foreign commercial borrowing from UBL Dubai and USD 942.71 million raised through Naya Pakistan Certificates, split between conventional and Islamic facilities. Furthermore, the country generated USD 2.95 billion via bond issuances in September, underlining the broader scope of external financial mobilization for the economy.

stories.title: CPPA-G Requests Rs3 Per Unit Adjustment for October Fuel Charges
stories.summary:
The Central Power Purchasing Agency - Guaranteed (CPPA-G) has requested a positive adjustment of approximately Rs 3 per unit for October 2026 under the monthly Fuel Charges Adjustment (FCA) mechanism. The proposed adjustment aims to gather an additional Rs 30 billion from consumers across distribution companies (Discos) and K-Electric (KE). The National Electric Power Regulator Authority (Nepra) is scheduled to conduct public hearings on November 26, 2026, to review this tariff modification request.

According to documentation provided to Nepra, total energy generated in October reached 10,744 GWh at a basket price of Rs 10.6277 per unit, accumulating a total energy cost of Rs 114.744 billion. Hydel generation contributed 2,818 GWh, representing 26.23 percent of the total output. Other sources included local coal at 1,360 GWh, imported coal at 1,569 GWh, high-speed diesel at 198 GWh, furnace oil at 351 GWh, gas-based generation at 1,090 GWh, and RLNG at 757 GWh. Furthermore, nuclear generation stood at 2,009 GWh, alongside 53 GWh imported from Iran, 42 GWh from bagasse, and 316 GWh from wind power.

The CPPA-G also factored in previous adjustments, supplemental charges, and transmission loss reductions. Net electricity supplied to Discos during the month totaled 10,352 GWh at a rate of Rs 10.7515 per unit, valuing Rs 111.296 billion. The agency justified the requested increase of Rs 2.8819 per unit by noting that actual fuel charges exceeded the reference fuel charges of Rs 7.8696 per unit.

stories.title: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif Calls for Comprehensive Maritime and Port Reforms
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif advocated for extensive reforms within the nation's ports and the Pakistan National Shipping Corporation (PNSC) during a meeting held on Tuesday. Emphasizing the expansion of cargo-handling capacity and modernized operations, he stated that these measures are critical to transforming the country into a prominent regional trade and transshipment hub. Government agencies involved in port management were instructed to collaborate to eliminate obstacles for businesses and expedite commercial activities.

The Prime Minister underscored the importance of streamlining cargo transportation, customs clearance procedures, and general port protocols to ease burdens on the business community and bolster economic growth. Regarding the PNSC, he demanded structural transformations to establish the state-owned shipping enterprise as a modern, financially resilient, and globally competitive entity. Officials were tasked with formulating a viable expansion strategy for the corporation's fleet to strengthen national import and export shipping capabilities.

During the briefing, attendees reviewed a business development plan for the PNSC focusing on fleet growth and human resource optimization. These initiatives aim to elevate maritime cargo capacity to international standards by the year 2030, reinforcing the trade infrastructure essential for the movement of goods.

The session gathered high-ranking officials including Minister for Economic Affairs Ahad Cheema, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, Maritime Affairs Minister Junaid Anwar Chaudhry, Privatisation Adviser Muhammad Ali, State Minister for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani, and Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Energy Lt Gen (retd) Zafar Iqbal, alongside parliamentarians Farooq Sattar and Abdul Qadir Patel.

stories.title: Pakistan and Turkmenistan Commit to Accelerating TAPI Gas Pipeline Project
stories.summary:
Pakistan and Turkmenistan have committed to accelerating the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India (TAPI) gas pipeline project, emphasizing the necessity of synchronized political engagement and coordinated actions to surmount technical, commercial, and security hurdles. This consensus emerged during the Sixth Session of the Pakistan-Turkmenistan Joint Intergovernmental Commission (JIC) in Islamabad on Tuesday, co-chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar and Turkmenistan’s Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers and Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov.

The talks encompassed bilateral cooperation spanning trade, investment, energy, agriculture, transport, IT, education, health, finance, tourism, and culture, with a strong emphasis on regional connectivity and business partnerships. The TAPI initiative, spanning 1,814 kilometers, is planned to deliver 33 billion cubic metres of natural gas annually from Turkmenistan's Galkynysh gas field to South Asia, serving as a cornerstone for regional energy security.

During a joint media briefing, Rashid Meredov highlighted plans to convene the TAPI Steering Committee and announced an upcoming second meeting of the Joint Working Group on Oil and Gas. Senator Ishaq Dar noted that the technical and commercial components of the pipeline require continuous political dialogue, while also mentioning discussions on a proposed electricity transmission project linking Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, and Pakistan.

Concluding the session, both nations signed the JIC Protocol, a 2026–2030 cooperation program for their foreign ministries, and a tourism memorandum of understanding. The ministers reaffirmed diplomacy as the sole method for resolving regional issues, with Meredov commending Pakistan's contributions to regional peace and stability.

stories.title: رحیم یار خان میں خودکشی کا ڈراما رچانے والا مطلوب ملزم گرفتار
stories.summary:
رحیم یار خان میں 42 روز قبل خودکشی کا جھوٹا ڈراما رچانے والے ملزم نعمان ریاض کو گرفتار کر لیا گیا ہے۔ پولیس کے مطابق مقروض ملزم نے ایک ویڈیو ریکارڈ کی تھی جس میں اس نے خودکشی کا اعلان کیا تھا اور اپنی کار کوٹ سمابہ نہر میں گرا کر روپوش ہوگیا تھا۔

اس دوران نہر سے ملزم کی گاڑی نکالنے کی کوشش میں ایک ریسکیو اہلکار ڈوب کر شہید ہو گیا تھا۔ جب ملزم کے اہل خانہ کو اس کی لاش نہ ملی تو انہوں نے نعمان ریاض کے اغوا کا مقدمہ درج کرا دیا تھا۔

اب ریسکیو اہلکار کی شہادت کا مقدمہ بھی نامزد ملزم کے خلاف درج کر لیا گیا ہے۔ ڈی پی او رحیم یار خان کا کہنا ہے کہ ملزم کے خلاف تمام تر قانونی کارروائی کا آغاز کر دیا گیا ہے۔

اس خبر کے علاوہ ملک بھر کے دیگر اہم سیاسی اور انتظامی امور بھی زیر بحث رہے۔ پی ٹی آئی ارکان نے صوبائی حکومت کی کارکردگی پر تحفظات کا اظہار کیا جبکہ پاک فضائیہ اور ترک فضائیہ کے حکام کے درمیان اہم ملاقات ہوئی۔ اس کے علاوہ کراچی کے علاقے لیاقت آباد سپر مارکیٹ میں ڈاکو پچیس لاکھ روپے سے زائد کی رقم لوٹ کر فرار ہو گئے۔

stories.title: Climate Negotiators Express Deep Divisions Over Sprawling COP31 Draft Deal
stories.summary:
Climate negotiators warned on Tuesday that an extensive and contentious draft COP31 agreement has established the groundwork for difficult discussions before the United Nations summit in Turkiye concludes later in the week. The 18-page "cover decision" draft, published by co-host Australia, encompasses a wide spectrum of demands ranging from calls to phase out fossil fuels to the defense of climate science and longstanding financial disputes. European Union climate envoy Wopke Hoekstra criticized the document in a speech in Antalya, stating that it risks distracting participants from crucial implementation goals and could make the entire process untenable.

Hookserta further remarked that the draft resembles a "shopping list" that reopens past debates, suggesting it requires significant modifications to move in the right direction. Other European officials dismissed the text as a "Christmas wish list" that attempts to satisfy everyone while ultimately pleasing no one. Australian Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who is steering the negotiations, acknowledged during the release of the document on Monday that the text contains elements lacking universal agreement, adding that at least one more draft will be introduced before the end of the week. Although talks are scheduled to conclude on Friday, climate negotiations frequently run into overtime because agreements require absolute consensus.

A Latin American official described the document as overly long and emphasized that time is running out. Another European negotiator criticized Australia's strategy as a "kitchen sink approach," noting a long journey ahead to reach a desired outcome. The draft includes a controversial proposal for wealthy nations to achieve net zero emissions by 2030, a target viewed by many as realistically unattainable. An official from a European country characterized the inclusion as tactical pressure from emerging countries on developed nations, pointing out that such demands are unacceptable to a bloc that includes Saudi Arabia and India.

The draft also features language concerning the phaseout of fossil fuels, which oil-producing nations have historically resisted. While Environment Minister Michael Joseph of Antigua and Barbuda expressed a desire for a commitment to phase out fossil fuels, he acknowledged that achieving consensus on the issue at COP31 will prove extremely difficult. Additionally, Saudi Arabia sits at the center of another dispute regarding the publication timeline for upcoming reports by the UN climate science panel. While dozens of European, African, and Pacific nations want the next Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change reports published ahead of a global carbon stocktake at COP33 in 2028, countries like Saudi Arabia and India are accused of pushing for a delay until 2029.

stories.title: PTI Questions Timing and Sincerity of Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari's System Critique
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf has responded to Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari's recent remarks regarding the collapse of the country's political system, questioning why it took him so long to acknowledge the severe hardships faced by ordinary citizens. In an official statement, PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram acknowledged that the PPP leader finally recognized public difficulties, but immediately challenged the sincerity of his statements given that the PPP forms part of the ruling coalition and shares responsibility for the ongoing political and economic crisis.

Akram highlighted that soaring flour prices, unaffordable electricity bills, and escalating petrol costs have rendered daily life increasingly difficult for the public. He asserted that the PPP cannot enjoy the privileges of being part of the government while simultaneously criticizing the very framework it helps sustain. According to the PTI official, the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz and the PPP bear joint responsibility for the country's economic conditions and cannot absolve themselves of accountability solely through political statements.

The PTI representative also directed criticism toward Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari's involvement in passing the controversial 26th Constitutional Amendment, asserting that the PPP chairman played a leading role in securing its approval. He claimed that the legislative measure dealt a severe blow to judicial independence and constitutional supremacy, making his party equally accountable for the subsequent consequences. This legislative legacy, he argued, binds the PPP to the failures of the current administration.

Turning to the issue of reserved parliamentary seats, Akram described the withholding of the PTI's mandated seats as a direct violation of democratic principles and a blatant disregard for the public electoral mandate. He challenged the PPP chairman to demonstrate genuine commitment to democracy by facilitating the return of those seats to the PTI. Concluding his statement, Akram emphasized that restoring the public's mandate, upholding the Constitution, and ensuring the rule of law remain absolute prerequisites for pulling the nation out of its current multidimensional crisis.

stories.title: Saudi Firm Signs Pact for $30 Billion Energy Project in Pakistan
stories.summary:
Saudi Arabian energy company Delta Energy Saudi has signed a preliminary agreement with Inter State Gas Systems of Pakistan to explore the development of regional energy infrastructure. The proposed initiative carries an estimated investment value of approximately $30 billion. Announced on Tuesday, the framework aims to evaluate a natural gas pipeline entering Pakistan through its western frontier and extending toward the Arabian Sea port of Gwadar in the country's south-west.

Additional components of the evaluation include potential extensions to Pakistan's eastern border, liquefied natural gas facilities, gas processing units, storage sites, and export terminals. The proposed blueprint also outlines a route originating from Chaman on the Afghan border and crossing Pakistan toward the Indian frontier near Fazilka. Delta Energy identified this specific pathway as a primary strategic commitment that requires formal accords with both Pakistani and Indian governments.

The initiative intends to source potential supplies from Afghanistan, including the Kashk gas concession, and is separate from the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India project without relying on Turkmenistan. Company representatives clarified that the signed accord merely establishes a mechanism for project assessment and does not equate to a binding financial commitment or final investment decision regarding construction.

The development matters as it sets the groundwork for extensive cross-border energy corridors aimed at bolstering supply networks in South Asia. Background details indicate that previous plans to introduce external gas pipelines into Pakistan have faced years of delays, highlighting the strategic complexity of regional energy integration.

stories.title: Pakistan Records $39 Million Current Account Surplus in October
stories.summary:
Pakistan achieved a current account surplus of $39 million in October, driven by rising dollar inflows and an expansion in the nation's foreign exchange reserves. This result marks a notable recovery from the preceding month, which registered a deficit of $371 million due to a widening trade gap fueled by higher global energy costs. Despite the higher import levels, the government maintained a free import policy to stimulate economic growth, which has stagnated at an average of about three percent over recent years.

Data released by the State Bank of Pakistan on Tuesday revealed that the cumulative current account deficit narrowed to $850 million during the first four months of the 2026-27 fiscal year. This compares favorably to a deficit of $1.062 billion recorded during the same period in the previous fiscal year. However, the broader trade deficit in goods and services widened significantly to $13.358 billion for the July-October period, up from $11.496 billion a year earlier, largely driven by increased imports of luxury items.

Foreign direct investment rose by 22 percent during the four-month window, reaching $935 million compared to $764 million in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year. Nevertheless, officials noted that these inflows remain modest compared to neighboring regional economies. The government attributed this restraint in foreign investment to ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Gulf region, which have amplified investor concerns regarding the stability of local financial and economic systems.

The figures provide vital insight into the nation's external economic health and fiscal trajectory. The data underscores the persistent challenge of balancing trade deficits and stimulating domestic growth amid external regional uncertainties.

stories.title: Middle East Conflict Worsens Inflation and External Outlook, Says SBP
stories.summary:
The ongoing Middle East conflict has adversely impacted inflation and the external economic outlook, according to the State Bank of Pakistan's annual report for 2025-26, released on Tuesday. To counteract secondary pressures and support macroeconomic stability, the central bank increased its policy rate by 100 basis points in April. Similar monetary tightening responses were observed globally as central banks paused rate cuts or raised rates in response to international shocks.

Pakistan's economic indicators demonstrated overall resilience throughout the 2026 fiscal year despite multiple challenges, including monsoon floods, trade tariff uncertainties from the United States, and regional conflicts that escalated global commodity prices. Average headline consumer price index inflation remained close to the upper bound of the medium-term target, foreign exchange reserves surpassed the $18 billion year-end target, and real gross domestic product achieved higher growth. The central bank conducted net forex purchases of $8.1 billion and reduced forward and swap liabilities by $1.6 billion.

Despite overall stability, average consumer price index inflation hovered at 5.5 percent between July and February, but surged into double digits starting in April due to sharp increases in global oil prices. Energy contributions to consumer inflation spiked significantly between March and June. Food inflation also climbed as a result of higher wheat prices driven by domestic supply constraints, while core inflation remained elevated following the transmission of production and transport cost increases.

The report underscores the vulnerability of domestic prices to international commodity shocks originating from geopolitical strife. It highlights the role of prudent monetary policies and fiscal consolidation in shielding the broader financial system, which saw improved depth through expanded private sector credit.

stories.title: Private DNA Test Cannot Override Child's Legitimacy, Lahore High Court Rules
stories.summary:
The Lahore High Court has ruled that a privately obtained DNA test cannot overturn the legal presumption of legitimacy for a child born during a valid marriage. Justice Asad Ali Bajwa delivered the verdict while upholding an enhanced maintenance award for a minor son against his father, Osama Tahir, who resides in the United Kingdom. The ruling stems from a legal challenge filed by the father against lower family court decisions regarding maintenance and dowry.

The legal dispute began when Zainab Irfan and her minor son filed a suit for maintenance, dower, and dowry articles following the breakdown of their marriage, which took place on August 18, 2019. Although a local family court initially awarded the minor child 10,000 rupees per month, an additional district and sessions judge subsequently raised the monthly allowance to 25,000 rupees with a 10 percent annual increase, alongside an award for the mother's iddat period and dowry items valued at 970,000 rupees. The father contested the paternity of the younger son, presenting a DNA report from a UK laboratory that claimed paternity was excluded.

Justice Bajwa rejected the petitioner's argument, emphasizing that under Article 128 of the Qanun-i-Shahadat Order of 1984, a birth occurring during a subsisting marriage serves as conclusive proof of legitimacy. The judge noted that witnesses confirmed the marriage was intact at the time of birth and that the father and paternal grandmother had accompanied the mother to the hospital. He stressed that unilateral DNA reports must be approached with caution and cannot displace statutory legal presumptions, with the welfare of the child remaining paramount.

The court also addressed the father's financial capacity, noting that witness testimonies confirmed he lived and earned abroad in the United Kingdom. Justice Bajwa ruled that maintenance must be determined based on the child's reasonable needs, including food, clothing, lodging, education, and healthcare, alongside the father's earning capacity. The judgment reinforces legal protections for children and families within Pakistan's judicial framework.

stories.title: Taliban Supreme Leader Makes Rare Kabul Appearance to Urge Obedience
stories.summary:
Hibatullah Akhundzada, the reclusive supreme leader of the Taliban, traveled from his base in Kandahar to the Afghan capital of Kabul on Tuesday for a rare public appearance. Speaking at a conference at Kabul University regarding the impact of his decrees, Akhundzada urged his audience to cultivate affection for him among the populace so that citizens would readily obey his rules. He emphasized that with the triumph of Islam and the establishment of an Islamic system under the authority of the Islamic Emirate, it is crucial to help people understand the true nature of the regime. Akhundzada has ruled Afghanistan by decree for over five years after inheriting the Taliban leadership a decade ago.

The leader's visit prompted an extensive security mobilization in Kabul. Journalists reported seeing snipers positioned on rooftops surrounding Kabul University, dozens of Humvees securing the gates, and intelligence personnel deployed throughout the area. Additionally, staff and students noted that Kabul University had been closed since Sunday, while local residents stated that their homes underwent searches by security forces. Thousands of attendees, including senior government officials and scholars, participated in the conference, according to the Ministry of Higher Education. Prior to Akhundzada's arrival, participants were instructed to hold hands and renew their pledge of allegiance to the supreme leader.

Akhundzada, whose age is estimated to be between 60 and 70, typically governs and communicates with the public through audio messages released by the government. Public appearances by the leader in Kabul are extremely uncommon, as he generally remains in Kandahar, the southern heartland of the Taliban movement. His decrees are formulated based on a strict interpretation of Islamic law. Furthermore, authorities have previously released only a single photograph of him showing a greying beard and a white turban, which was captured more than twenty years ago.

stories.title: Punjab Minister Azma Bokhari Dismisses Imran Khan Medical Claims as Propaganda
stories.summary:
Punjab Minister for Information and Culture Azma Bokhari has stated that former Prime Minister Imran Khan's recent letters regarding his health are merely propaganda and that he has sought a written National Reconciliation Ordinance (NRO) under his signature. Bokhari asserted that complaints concerning inadequate prison medical facilities are baseless, noting that the former premier has received extensive medical attention during his detention at Adiala Jail.

According to Bokhari, prison staff check Imran Khan's vital signs three times daily, and he has been examined by medical specialists on eight separate occasions. Detailed evaluations have involved various medical boards and prominent doctors, including Dr Arif Khan, Dr Farqad Alamgir, Dr Nadeem Qureshi, and Dr Akhtar Ali Bandesha, alongside his personal physicians Dr Asim Yousaf and Dr Faisal Sultan. Notable medical interventions cited include checkups by a cardiologist in August 2024, an eye and blood pressure examination by a five-member team in February 2026, medication adjustments by a four-member board in August 2026, and temporary transfers to PIMS for specialized eye treatments including an Anti-VEGF injection.

Bokhari further dismissed allegations made by Bushra Bibi regarding pests and snakes in her cell as entirely fabricated. She remarked that the claims likely stemmed from mistaking common earthworms, which emerge during the monsoon season, for reptiles, noting that prison authorities immediately rejected these court petitions.

The minister emphasized that the medical care provided to Imran Khan in jail surpasses the facilities afforded to any other prisoner in Pakistan. She contrasted his current complaints with his past behavior, alleging that a man who once mocked the illnesses of others is now raising health concerns while facing the legal consequences of his own actions.

stories.title: Sindh Secretary Faisal Ahmed Uqaili Highlights Climate Strategies at COP31
stories.summary:
Sindh Environment and Climate Change Secretary Faisal Ahmed Uqaili presented the provincial government's climate initiatives at the COP31 conference in Turkiye. Representing Sindh, Uqaili participated in sessions covering Delta Blue Carbon, eco-friendly brick kilns, and energy futures, while also chairing related discussions to showcase regional efforts in cutting air pollution, fostering carbon markets, and drawing foreign investment.

Uqaili pointed out that Sindh previously operated around 600 conventional brick kilns impacting approximately 160,000 nearby residents. To mitigate environmental harm, the province mandated the adoption of zigzag technology. Four traditional kilns have already transitioned to this modern method, yielding a 53 percent drop in air pollution, a 24 percent decrease in fuel consumption, and an 87 percent increase in brick strength.

To drive financial growth in green sectors, the environment department has established a specialized unit dedicated to advancing carbon markets and encouraging international investments. Officials are currently steering 13 carbon market initiatives and six priority climate projects, which encompass riverine forests, biogas generation, and methane recovery. Additionally, the Sindh Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA) deployed a digital monitoring system to bolster environmental oversight.

Concluding his address at the international conference, Uqaili urged global investors to explore economic opportunities within Sindh's expanding portfolio of climate projects. Conference participants responded favorably, expressing appreciation for the provincial government's structured approach to environmental protection and carbon emission reduction.

stories.title: Experts Stress Media's Role in Health, Nutrition, and Diabetes Awareness
stories.summary:
The concluding day of a two-stage international conference on Nutrition, Health and Diabetes took place at the Indus Hotel in Hyderabad. Organized jointly by the University of Sindh’s Institute of Biochemistry and the Asian Institute of Medical Sciences, the event featured research paper presentations and expert recommendations from national and international specialists.

Prof. Dr. Fateh Muhammad Marri, Vice Chancellor of the University of Sindh and chief guest of the event, delivered an address warning against the proliferation of health misinformation on social media, which he noted often inflicts harm rather than providing value. He underscored that accurate data is vital for disease prevention and advised the public to rely strictly on the guidance of qualified medical professionals for managing diabetes and other conditions. He called for expanded public awareness campaigns across print, electronic, and social media platforms, as well as through academic seminars.

Highlighting the connection between diet and physical well-being, the Vice Chancellor stated that poor and unbalanced nutrition severely impairs children's growth and height, rendering them susceptible to illnesses. Organizers Prof. Dr. Afsheen Shah, Director of the Institute of Biochemistry, and Prof. Dr. Sadiq Memon of the Asian Institute of Medical Sciences expressed gratitude to visiting scholars for their participation and outlined the core goals of the gathering.

Several international experts contributed specialized insights during the sessions. Dr. Syed Kashif Hussain Kazmi traveled from the United Kingdom to discuss evolving trends in diabetes, while Dr. Khalid Mumtaz arrived from the United States to lecture on the origins and treatments of liver diseases. Additional presentations were delivered by Dr. S.M. Wasim Jafri, who examined diabetes alongside fatty liver conditions, and Dr. Abdul Basit, who analyzed distinct variations of diabetes prevalent across South Asia.

stories.title: Saylani Welfare Launches Mining and Minerals Training Division for Youth
stories.summary:
Saylani Welfare International Trust has launched a dedicated Mining and Minerals Division, replicating the structure of its existing IT training programs to prepare young individuals from Balochistan and other provinces for careers in Pakistan's mineral sector. The inaugural phase will train a batch of 60 youths from Balochistan in Karachi before sending them back to their home districts for hands-on, field-based instruction.

The initiative follows Saylani's appearance at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum in Islamabad, where a 10-member delegation attended on a special government invitation. Led by Founder and Chairman Maulana Muhammad Bashir Farooq Qadri, the organization displayed its work at a complimentary exhibition stall that attracted significant interest from local and international attendees.

During the investment forum, organization leaders briefed high-level officials—including Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, Field Marshal General Asim Munir, provincial chief ministers, and foreign delegates from over 60 countries—on strategies to equip marginalized youth with vocational skills. Maulana Bashir Farooq emphasized that the new division aims to meet the rising demand for skilled technical labor while securing employment prospects for youth within their native regions.

To solidify the initiative, Saylani Welfare signed Memorandums of Understanding with three entities: the Heavy Mechanical Complex (HTMA), the All Mine Association, and Komatsu. These partnerships will focus on developing industry-aligned training curricula and vocational programs. With the initial selection of 60 Balochistan trainees finalized, the organization is set to begin the Karachi-based training phase immediately before deploying participants for regional practical work.

stories.title: Sindh Chief Secretary Launches New Digital Domicile and PRC Portal
stories.summary:
The Chief Secretary of Sindh, Asif Haider Shah, officially inaugurated a new e-Domicile and Permanent Residence Certificate (PRC) portal in Karachi. The newly introduced digital platform and accompanying mobile application eliminate the traditional requirement for citizens to wait in long physical queues, allowing individuals to complete their applications directly from home.

According to the chief secretary, processes that previously required weeks to finalize can now be completed within a matter of hours. Furthermore, the electronic system is designed to stop fraudulent applications and fake domiciles, while the increased accessibility is expected to enhance public perception of the government.

During the launch event, Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi outlined the core functionalities of the portal, noting that it incorporates user registration, facial recognition, and document uploading tools. Applicants can pay the required fee through an online transaction or a bank challan, and they are able to track their application progress directly on the platform until the relevant Deputy Commissioner's office reaches a final decision.

Following the inauguration, Chief Secretary Asif Haider Shah personally handed out domiciles to young applicants who successfully utilized the digital system. He also announced that the e-domicile facility will soon be expanded to encompass other districts throughout the province of Sindh.

stories.title: Former Business Recorder Sub-Editor M. Akhtar Bashir Passes Away
stories.summary:
M. Akhtar Bashir, a former sub-editor for the publication Business Recorder, has passed away at the age of 82. His death was reported by the publication yesterday in Karachi.

He is survived by his grieving family, including his wife, three sons, and one daughter. The community and former colleagues mourn the loss of the veteran journalist.

Funeral services for the late sub-editor were held yesterday. His Namaz-e-Janaza took place at the Banori Town Masjid located in Karachi.

stories.title: K-Electric Denies Excess Power Outages in Karachi Commercial Hubs
stories.summary:
Utility provider K-Electric (KE) has formally denied allegations of implementing excessive load shedding across several major commercial and wholesale markets in Karachi. The disputed areas include Jodia Bazar, the Pakistan Motorcycle Spare Parts Importers and Dealers Association, Auto Parts Market, Eidgah, Urdu Bazar, and Old Haji Camp.

These commercial districts are powered by a total of 15 electricity feeders. The company noted that the vast majority of these feeders fall into high-loss categories, where combined technical and commercial losses span between 40 percent and nearly 90 percent. KE emphasized that supplying free electricity to any region is completely unfeasible, noting that over 70 percent of its overall service territory network remains entirely free from load shedding.

KE explained that power interruptions are driven by distinct factors, requiring differentiation between scheduled load shedding, localized technical faults, and infrastructure damage caused by non-utility incidents. Actual load-shedding schedules are directly tied to local electricity theft and non-payment rates, following published timetables available on the utility's official website.

Additionally, the provider pointed out that widespread urban development work has severely compromised its network integrity. Unsanctioned excavations and pickaxing have frequently damaged underground cables, triggering unplanned outages across Karachi. The company encourages consumers to report disruptions through official complaint channels and utilize the KE Live App to monitor estimated restoration times transparently.

stories.title: Medical Experts Sound Alarm Over Pakistan's Escalating Diabetes Crisis
stories.summary:
Medical professionals have raised serious concerns regarding the soaring rates of diabetes in Pakistan during a World Diabetes Day seminar at Ziauddin University. Titled "Early Action on Diabetes: A Solution for a Healthier Future," the event was organized by Ziauddin University's Department of Medicine and College of Molecular Medicine, alongside the Department of Family Medicine and the Pakistan Endocrine Society.

Prof. Dr. Muhammad Ali Shaikh, Vice Chancellor of Ziauddin University, stated that Pakistan now ranks among the top countries globally for diabetic patients, calling the situation an alarming public health crisis. Consultant Endocrinologist and Pakistan Endocrine Society President Dr. Ali Asghar warned that focusing strictly on blood sugar ignores vital organ damage, noting that one in three diabetics already suffers from chronic kidney disease, while heart disease remains the primary killer across these overlapping conditions.

Prof. Dr. Uzma Ghori highlighted that 34.5 million individuals are affected, meaning one in every three adults in Pakistan suffers from diabetes, giving the country the highest percentage burden globally. Meanwhile, Prof. Dr. Najmul Islam of Aga Khan University Hospital stressed the importance of proper clinical management to achieve glycemic control and mitigate long-term health complications.

Prof. Dr. Fatima Jehangir addressed the broader "diabesity" crisis affecting 70 million people, pointing out that 82 million adults live with a high body mass index. She warned that unmanaged obesity could drive Pakistan toward economic and public health collapse, with the country projected to rank fifth globally in obesity by 2030 and face economic impacts reaching US$51 billion. Concluding the seminar, Prof. Dr. Talat Mirza emphasized that advancing molecular and clinical research into early diagnostics is vital to overcoming the epidemic.

stories.title: SSUET hosts awareness summit to promote breast cancer prevention and care
stories.summary:
Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology recently hosted an event known as the Trifecta of Health Awareness Summit. The gathering was organized by the university's Department of Biomedical Engineering and Allied Health Sciences alongside Darul Sehat Hospital, PASTIC, and the European Union project BIOMED 5.0 to mark Breast Cancer Day and educate the community on prevention and treatment.

Erum Akbar Ali Khan, Chairperson of the Zakir Ali Khan Foundation and Chief Guest at the event, stressed that early detection is crucial and noted that men joining female health advocacy strengthens the movement. University Chancellor Muhammad Akbar Ali Khan emphasized that education empowers women to handle the disease with courage, while Vice Chancellor Prof. Dr. Muhammad Aamir highlighted that women's health is essential for family and societal well-being.

Several experts spoke during the program. Prof. Dr. Qudsia Tariq from Karachi University addressed mental well-being, Dr. Eraj Humayun from NED University spoke about DNA Day and genetic innovations, Dr. Sarah Rauf from Darul Sehat Hospital delivered a talk on breast cancer awareness, and Prof. Dr. Asima Faisal of DUHA gave a special address.

The initiative matters because it brings experts and community members together to emphasize that timely diagnosis, accurate information, and regular screenings save lives and foster a supportive environment for patients.

stories.title: Boiler explosion triggers major fire at food factory in Baldia Town
stories.summary:
A major fire erupted at a food factory situated in Rashidabad, near Baldia Town within Karachi, which is the capital of Sindh. The blaze began on the ground floor of the building due to a boiler explosion.

Upon receiving alerts, fire brigade and rescue teams rapidly arrived at the location to initiate relief operations. Officials from Rescue 1122 confirmed that the explosion quickly caused the fire to engulf the entire structure and intensify, posing a serious threat of spreading further.

Immediate concerns arose because a garments factory stands directly next to the burning food factory, creating a risk that the flames could reach the adjacent building. Authorities deployed eight fire engines and one snorkel to the site to fight the blaze.

Firefighters and rescue workers engaged in strenuous efforts to contain the fire, prevent further expansion, and avoid major casualties. While cooling and firefighting operations continued, officials noted that it would take time to fully extinguish the flames.

stories.title: Alkhidmat Karachi launches 27th Help Centre offering free medical equipment
stories.summary:
Alkhidmat Karachi has officially opened its 27th Help Centre located in Korangi J Area. The new facility aims to provide free medical equipment and various other welfare services to local residents.

Naveed Ali Baig, the Chief Executive of Alkhidmat Karachi, inaugurated the centre during a ceremony attended by local dignitaries, area residents, and officials including Ameer Jamaat-e-Islami Korangi District Mirza Farhan Baig, Director Community Services Umar Qaim Khani, and Senior Manager Sarfaraz Sheikh. During the gathering, Naveed Ali Baig noted that the citywide network of 27 centres provides roughly 140 essential items.

Citizens can borrow items such as oxygen cylinders, crutches, walkers, patient beds, suction machines, and nebulisers free of charge for a specified period and return them when they are no longer needed. Additionally, the Korangi facility will offer a subsidised funeral transport or Mayyat Bus service for the community.

Director Community Services Umar Qaim Khani highlighted other year-round welfare initiatives, such as dowry and winter packages, ration distributions during Ramazan, meat distributions on Eid-ul-Azha, and a recently completed citywide fumigation campaign against dengue and malaria. The centre matters because it delivers vital health and social support to deserving citizens.

stories.title: FBR establishes minimum export values for various sesame seed varieties
stories.summary:
The Federal Board of Revenue has set minimum customs export values for different types of sesame seeds, with prices ranging from USD 1,103 to USD 1,524 per metric ton. The Directorate of Customs Valuation in Lahore issued Valuation Ruling No. 03 of 2026 to specify these minimum free-on-board values for export consignments.

Under the ruling, hybrid, farm, till, natural, and mixed sesame seed varieties have a minimum export value of USD 1,103 per metric tonne. White and black Sortex seeds are priced at USD 1,211 per metric tonne, while hulled sesame seeds are assessed at USD 1,524 per metric tonne. The ruling also introduces updated Pakistan Customs Tariff codes for integration into the WeBOC system, assigning specific subcodes for the different seed categories.

The valuation process was launched following directions from the Director General of Customs Valuation in Karachi.
